尽管财政收入减少，但地方政府的[刚性支出](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E5%88%9A%E6%80%A7%E6%94%AF%E5%87%BA&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLliJrmgKfmlK_lh7oiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.6pXzHb7RQmqNzkRXuLZEaLfbIBbgtK0y_koce2Oh6VA&zhida_source=entity)并未减少，反而在某些领域有所增加，例如社会保障支出、债务付息支出等刚性支出。这使得地方政府在[财政支出](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E8%B4%A2%E6%94%BF%E6%94%AF%E5%87%BA&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLotKLmlL_mlK_lh7oiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.iZb4Dk4W2wz0QFkwUfP_-kyM4TfqJH3I1qO100678Ko&zhida_source=entity)上面临更大的压力，尤其是在需要进行大规模基础设施建设和公共服务提供的情况下，地方财政更显得捉襟见肘。财政收入减少、支出压力增大、债务偿还压力、财政收支缺口扩大、[融资](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E8%9E%8D%E8%B5%84&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLono3otYQiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.hsSARi6x5pdBLjGPCS2gE4kQ73PYDj8112IXEVvfltc&zhida_source=entity)难度增加以及[经济结构调整](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E7%BB%8F%E6%B5%8E%E7%BB%93%E6%9E%84%E8%B0%83%E6%95%B4&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLnu4_mtY7nu5PmnoTosIPmlbQiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.Nd1uIH_RBqnJU-DWe88MOIdwcLx2AAYpHEZOnAmLH4g&zhida_source=entity)，这些压力不仅影响了地方政府的[财政收支](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=2&q=%E8%B4%A2%E6%94%BF%E6%94%B6%E6%94%AF&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLotKLmlL_mlLbmlK8iLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MiwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.2qerknyq6GJVYz9wzJd9tEe_wKLNjJMK3nKckAhHlJI&zhida_source=entity)，还可能对地方经济和社会发展产生深远的影响。

**土地财政依赖度被动性减弱**

受土地出让收入下滑等因素影响，土地财政依赖度也发生了明显变化。从整体数据看，2021年全国土地出让收入87051亿元，[政府基金性收入](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E6%94%BF%E5%BA%9C%E5%9F%BA%E9%87%91%E6%80%A7%E6%94%B6%E5%85%A5&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLmlL_lupzln7rph5HmgKfmlLblhaUiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.DCTQ0F2qJ8YsOS7hMCcwcUUMSJWPvYbnL8DDVP7LrBY&zhida_source=entity)98024亿元，一般公共预算收入202539亿元，如果按照“[土地出让收入](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=7&q=%E5%9C%9F%E5%9C%B0%E5%87%BA%E8%AE%A9%E6%94%B6%E5%85%A5&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLlnJ_lnLDlh7rorqnmlLblhaUiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6NywiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.woewXnCfjGP6TejOob2twzw18OjUjax8ZVW3i3iiEzY&zhida_source=entity)/（政府基金性收入+[一般公共预算收入](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=2&q=%E4%B8%80%E8%88%AC%E5%85%AC%E5%85%B1%E9%A2%84%E7%AE%97%E6%94%B6%E5%85%A5&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLkuIDoiKzlhazlhbHpooTnrpfmlLblhaUiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MiwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.uirpSh2TRvgfpgajjGtv1k66JU8eCL3rR19BlocOpvk&zhida_source=entity)）”计算土地[财政依赖度](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=3&q=%E8%B4%A2%E6%94%BF%E4%BE%9D%E8%B5%96%E5%BA%A6&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLotKLmlL_kvp3otZbluqYiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MywiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.x7mnIH4nu9yOdBA9R5VVXKE9FMZpjAZKnk2OLcCFlbI&zhida_source=entity)，那么2021年的土地财政依赖度为28.96%；至2024年，全国土地出让金收入为48699亿元，政府基金性收入62090亿元，一般公共预算收入219702亿元，对应的土地财政依赖度为17.28%。土地财政依赖度整体水平3年下降11.68个百分点。

分省份看，江苏、贵州、湖北、[重庆](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E9%87%8D%E5%BA%86&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLph43luoYiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.vaTN50wgnB1Z31ywxO_Ui5PtaKb13EIv7KtSDU3CrTo&zhida_source=entity)、四川、福建、浙江、山东的地方财政对土地依赖度相对较高；部分省市的土地财政依赖度低、且土地出让收入同比出现正向增长，如黑龙江、新疆、[宁夏](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E5%AE%81%E5%A4%8F&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLlroHlpI8iLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.8Irai2G558xvHv1MQc_AF6PKrvz4mv5gcvsSKyPOfEQ&zhida_source=entity)、云南和[天津](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E5%A4%A9%E6%B4%A5&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLlpKnmtKUiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.LJt2iuXXlYAovfVmWQevJiQHolslGm3SvBycLuTkfUU&zhida_source=entity)等地。

2020年，南方省份（如江苏、浙江、海南、四川、福建）土地财政依赖度普遍较高，部分省份土地出让金占[政府性基金收入](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E6%94%BF%E5%BA%9C%E6%80%A7%E5%9F%BA%E9%87%91%E6%94%B6%E5%85%A5&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLmlL_lupzmgKfln7rph5HmlLblhaUiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.RzYW3zsFKo8yK6Z7nA8xNr0Pjit8qdSxJ_PbZVyAKxk&zhida_source=entity)比例超过50%；北方省份（如山西、黑龙江）依赖度较低，主要依赖[一般预算收入](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E4%B8%80%E8%88%AC%E9%A2%84%E7%AE%97%E6%94%B6%E5%85%A5&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLkuIDoiKzpooTnrpfmlLblhaUiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.hCQAlv7Z1d6gu4_ogNuJ1_pQTut0ay7cfUQO_C0vLlA&zhida_source=entity)。进入2024年，各省份土地财政依赖度整体下降，但区域分化加剧。例如江苏、浙江等传统依赖土地财政的省份，因土地出让收入下滑，依赖度显著降低。仅福州、济南等少数城市依赖度逆势上升。

分城市看，核心城市依赖度骤降。一线城市土地财政依赖度普遍低于25%，深圳甚至低至2%；二线城市分化加剧，仅少数城市依赖度逆势增长，二线城市中杭州、南京等依赖度降至30%~50%，较2020年的高位明显收缩。三四线城市中，芜湖、广安、宜宾、宜昌等地级市，土地出让收入占政府基金性收入比值仍在70%以上，成为土地财政依赖度最高的典型代表。

值得注意的是，行政级别与[财政结构](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E8%B4%A2%E6%94%BF%E7%BB%93%E6%9E%84&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLotKLmlL_nu5PmnoQiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.7aBns0HDEibKAIHnSIdHJb8q5PgqT-dV0iwHXxfLA2w&zhida_source=entity)存在强关联性。四个直辖市中，北京、上海依托强大的产业基础，土地出让金占政府性基金收入比重维持在15%~20%区间，而重庆因特殊的地理经济条件，该比例长期高于50%。副省级城市群体呈现分化态势，深圳、广州等经济强市保持30%~40%，武汉、西安等中西部城市则普遍超过60%。

**破解土地财政依赖的路径**

随着房地产市场的周期性调整，商品房用地需求逐渐减弱，土地市场规模将进一步压缩。如何弥补土地财政留下的财政缺口成为亟待破解的难题。结合地方实践和专家给出的建议，可行性路径大致有以下几个方面：

首先，稳住房地产市场基本盘。房地产高速增长时代已经结束，但并不意味着房地产市场需求的枯竭。我国[新型城镇化](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E6%96%B0%E5%9E%8B%E5%9F%8E%E9%95%87%E5%8C%96&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLmlrDlnovln47plYfljJYiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.jeixxx1NrOJHRo0R871Faa-3EQBKtiAyektfrH4gwXM&zhida_source=entity)还有很大发展空间，刚性住房需求和改善性住房需求依然强劲。一线城市和强二线城市由于人口的持续流入，住房需求仍存在较大缺口。此前由于土地出让中实施的诸如限价、限面积、限容积率等限制性措施，市场上中高端住宅和“好房子”供应严重不足，随着“好房子”标准的出台和各种限制性措施的进一步解除，改善性住房需求迫切，“好房子”用地需求旺盛，并对土地市场形成有效支撑。房地产进入存量时代，大批老旧小区和危旧房需要更新改造，大量商业和产业用地需要盘活，这些都是未来土地市场新的增长机会。经历3年的市场调整，[房地产开发投资](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E6%88%BF%E5%9C%B0%E4%BA%A7%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%91%E6%8A%95%E8%B5%84&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLmiL_lnLDkuqflvIDlj5HmipXotYQiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.Rp1smzYTmByPucpttX2X4bQD920rwECrmM_SgJ7_r8I&zhida_source=entity)、商品房销售等指标将在合理区间内得到有效支撑并趋于稳定，土地出让收入仍是地方政府必不可少的财政收入来源。

2025年中央将“持续用地促进房地产市场止跌回稳”作为经济工作重要目标，并出台了一揽子增量政策，政策效果开始显现，但实现房地产市场止跌回稳还需要更大力度的政策支持。在稳定房地产市场方面，粤开证券首席[经济学家](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E7%BB%8F%E6%B5%8E%E5%AD%A6%E5%AE%B6&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLnu4_mtY7lrablrrYiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.BUSTW_yD9Re9o37QVe2YZEF1jRR4rbXdEWvm6oMs9kw&zhida_source=entity)罗志恒建议，要尽快采取保供给、促需求和稳房价举措，大力盘活闲置土地和收购存量房用于保障房，一线城市核心地段尽快推出高品质商品房，满足居民多层次住房需求。中央层面可成立“[房地产稳定基金](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E6%88%BF%E5%9C%B0%E4%BA%A7%E7%A8%B3%E5%AE%9A%E5%9F%BA%E9%87%91&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLmiL_lnLDkuqfnqLPlrprln7rph5EiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.SMWsOWlaSrmIu9rC6UT4SUSGg9oVuhauSpGSOIdW5Bg&zhida_source=entity)”，规模在2万亿元左右，专项用于保交楼、收储存量房和房企存量闲置土地等，同时减轻地方政府稳楼市压力，保障地方财政稳健运行。

其次，积极化解地方债务风险。随着土地财政红利消退，依靠土地市场抵押举债和卖地收入还债的模式难以为继，地方债务风险显性化与公共财政支出需求不断扩大的矛盾凸显。3月28日，财政部公开了最新的地方[政府债务](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E6%94%BF%E5%BA%9C%E5%80%BA%E5%8A%A1&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLmlL_lupzlgLrliqEiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.AQgMJ6BTilFVZDaxLQAo23E9152H4xmpPcqp6juhxP0&zhida_source=entity)余额情况，截至今年2月末，全国地方政府债务余额49.29万亿元，相较于2023年末增长超过20%。在化解地方债务方面，2024年11月8日，十四届全国人大常委会第十二次会议通过了“6+4+2”万亿元地方化债方案，12万亿元的总额度也成为近年来力度最大的化债方案。通过化债方案的实施，地方政府债务风险和偿债压力得到有效缓解，财政空间得到释放，增强了地方经济发展动能。

再次，通过扩展新税源破解土地财政困局。地方政府可结合产业升级、[资产盘活](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E8%B5%84%E4%BA%A7%E7%9B%98%E6%B4%BB&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLotYTkuqfnm5jmtLsiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.Rlx_xOff3yxVgvHM79-ptokEOuUfDOEsxNhFwHqM4zs&zhida_source=entity)等多维度创新，构建多元化税源体系。在产业升级方面，重点发展人工智能、新能源等战略性新型产业，拓展新的税源。例如杭州通过数字经济[产业集群](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E4%BA%A7%E4%B8%9A%E9%9B%86%E7%BE%A4&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLkuqfkuJrpm4bnvqQiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.eJpdeuKRCpfM7w9gU6GVtVQNAfi0X2oUTlEd7fXIPVo&zhida_source=entity)，2024年数字经济核心产业增加值占GDP比重达27%，贡献税收超30%；深圳试点碳税征收后年增收约12亿元；苏州工业园区通过生物医药产业链培育，2024年相关产业税收同比增长23%；位于中西部的贵州依托资源禀赋发展特色税源，[大数据](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E5%A4%A7%E6%95%B0%E6%8D%AE&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLlpKfmlbDmja4iLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.yow89Al5HbQrNhvaTquNdJ1rua451ATmUnN_xKUmSaM&zhida_source=entity)产业税收占比从2018年的3.7%提升至2024年的11.2%，成为地方政府重要税源。

最后，推动财税体制改革势在必行。长期来看，通过税制改革重构[地方税](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E5%9C%B0%E6%96%B9%E7%A8%8E&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLlnLDmlrnnqI4iLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.IqINaurJbjnVHuq78JwIjmYUGsqoAr3ynBth5dSMobA&zhida_source=entity)体系是解决地方土地财政依赖的重要一环。在财税体制改革方面罗志恒也给出了很好的建议：一是上收部分事权和支出责任到中央和省级政府，包括社保、食品药品监督管理、环境保护等事权上移，减轻地方政府的支出压力；二是统筹[消费税](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E6%B6%88%E8%B4%B9%E7%A8%8E&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLmtojotLnnqI4iLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.bt0jWL52tGFzx-fwDJMkvXx0liuCRvyCBzUKoW0UoDw&zhida_source=entity)征收环节后移和逐步换转给地方，补充土地出让收入下行对地方财力的冲击；三是完善[增值税抵扣](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E5%A2%9E%E5%80%BC%E7%A8%8E%E6%8A%B5%E6%89%A3&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLlop7lgLznqI7mirXmiaMiLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.lW8-bd_uKJUXTYwkkttr7LlaNiRS04dNdMtD11fp5T4&zhida_source=entity)链条，逐步清理不规范、不合理的增值税优惠政策；四是将[城市维护建设税](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E5%9F%8E%E5%B8%82%E7%BB%B4%E6%8A%A4%E5%BB%BA%E8%AE%BE%E7%A8%8E&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLln47luILnu7TmiqTlu7rorr7nqI4iLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.kWa8rl9YkSvRp0AAXOng5ifVSVsuGgeEYTe_NbP_wuI&zhida_source=entity)、教育费附加、地方教育附加合并为地方附加税；五是探索[国有资产](https://zhida.zhihu.com/search?content_id=256469247&content_type=Article&match_order=1&q=%E5%9B%BD%E6%9C%89%E8%B5%84%E4%BA%A7&zd_token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJpc3MiOiJ6aGlkYV9zZXJ2ZXIiLCJleHAiOjE3ODcwMTgwMDMsInEiOiLlm73mnInotYTkuqciLCJ6aGlkYV9zb3VyY2UiOiJlbnRpdHkiLCJjb250ZW50X2lkIjoyNTY0NjkyNDcsImNvbnRlbnRfdHlwZSI6IkFydGljbGUiLCJtYXRjaF9vcmRlciI6MSwiemRfdG9rZW4iOm51bGx9.3am1VCIrMorahzImMDZIzFlzr-2j6Pjz7OWMr9xfB8Y&zhida_source=entity)及其相关收入在中央与地方政府之间的划分机制，缓解地方政府对土地财政的过度依赖。

This is an article by 中国房地产报 (China Real Estate News) published on Zhihu on April 16, 2025, authored by 苏志勇 of the 城市与区域治理研究院 (Urban and Regional Governance Research Institute). The article analyzes how local governments in China can break through fiscal difficulties as their reliance on land finance (土地财政) weakens.

KEY FACTS:
- Land market in core first- and second-tier cities has recently warmed with a "地王潮" (wave of land king records), signaling stabilization of the real estate market, but this does not constitute a substantive reversal.
- National land transfer fee revenue (土地出让金) peaked at 8.7 trillion yuan (87051亿元) in 2021, then declined for 3 consecutive years to 4.87 trillion yuan (48699亿元) in 2024 — a 44% drop from the peak. 2024 declined 16% year-on-year.
- In 2024, 22 of 29 provinces reported negative growth in land transfer revenue. Jiangsu fell 23.3%, Zhejiang 27.0%, Guangdong 28.9%, Hunan 36.1%.
- 12 provinces saw declines exceeding 50% from historical highs: Qinghai -83.4%, Heilongjiang -72.8%, Gansu -68.1%, Guangdong -66.2%, Yunnan -64.7%, Shanxi -63.0%, Hunan -59.5%, Henan -58.0%.
- Top 10 provinces by land transfer revenue in 2024: Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Shandong, Sichuan, Shanghai, Guangdong, Hubei, Beijing, Fujian, Guizhou.
- In Q1 2025, national land transfer revenue reached 0.58 trillion yuan, up 11.33% year-on-year, with average premium rate of 9.81% (up 5.47 percentage points). Beijing, Hangzhou, Shanghai, Chengdu, Suzhou led in transaction amounts.
- Nearly 80% of prefecture-level cities had land transfer revenue under 1 billion yuan in Q1.
- Land finance dependency ratio (土地出让收入/(政府基金性收入+一般公共预算收入)) fell from 28.96% in 2021 to 17.28% in 2024 — a decline of 11.68 percentage points.
- First-tier cities have land finance dependency below 25% (Shenzhen as low as 2%). Hangzhou and Nanjing dropped to 30-50%. Fourth-tier cities like Wuhu, Guang'an, Yibin, Yichang still exceed 70% dependency.
- 自然资源部 (Ministry of Natural Resources) required cities with inventory clearing cycles exceeding 36 months to suspend new residential land sales.

FOUR PROPOSED PATHS TO BREAK THE DILEMMA:
1. Stabilize the real estate market — support housing demand, promote "好房子" (quality homes), urban renewal of old communities. 粤开证券 (Yuekai Securities) chief economist 罗志恒 recommended establishing a ~2 trillion yuan "房地产稳定基金" (Real Estate Stabilization Fund) for guaranteed delivery, purchasing existing stock for affordable housing, and idle land revitalization.
2. Resolve local debt risks — as of end-February 2025, national local government debt balance was 49.29 trillion yuan, up over 20% from end-2023. The November 8, 2024 "6+4+2" trillion yuan debt resolution plan (12 trillion yuan total) was the largest in recent years.
3. Expand new tax sources — develop strategic emerging industries (AI, new energy). Examples: Hangzhou's digital economy core industry contributed 27% of GDP and 30%+ of tax in 2024; Shenzhen's carbon tax pilot generates ~1.2 billion yuan annually; Suzhou Industrial Park biopharma tax up 23% in 2024; Guizhou's big data industry tax share rose from 3.7% (2018) to 11.2% (2024).
4. Advance fiscal/tax system reform — 罗志恒 proposed: (a) shift some expenditure responsibilities (social security, food/drug supervision, environmental protection) to central/provincial governments; (b) shift consumption tax collection to local governments; (c) clean up VAT deductions and preferential policies; (d) merge urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges into a local surtax; (e) explore state-owned asset revenue sharing mechanisms between central and local governments.

研究主题：中国中央和地方政府为应对房地产下行导致的财政压力所采取的政策措施及其效果评估（2021-2025）。

请提供一份详细的研究报告，使用中文，涵盖以下内容：

1. 转移支付：分析中央对地方转移支付的规模和结构变化（2021年至2025年），包括一般性转移支付和专项转移支付的年度规模，以及2023年增发1万亿元国债用于支持地方灾后重建和基建的政策细节。

2. 债务管理与置换：详细梳理2023年10月以来中央推动的地方政府债务化解（一揽子化债）政策，包括特殊再融资债券发行规模（累计约1.5万亿元至4万亿元的区间，请核实）、2024年11月人大批准的增加6万亿元地方政府债务限额置换存量隐性债务的政策（分三年实施，每年2万亿元）、以及新增专项债券每年4万亿元左右的发行规模和用途变化。

3. 税制改革与财政体制改革：梳理正在推进或拟议的相关改革，包括：
   - 房地产税立法（房产税改革试点）的最新进展和方向。
   - 消费税征收环节后移并下划地方的政策（2024年7月三中全会决定）。
   - 土地增值税、耕地占用税等的调整。
   - 中央与地方财政事权和支出责任划分改革。

4. 土地政策调整：分析地方政府在土地供给侧的应对，包括减少土地供应、调整土地出让节奏、城市更新与存量盘活政策等。

5. 效果评估：评估上述各项措施的实际效果，包括：
   - 化债措施是否有效缓解了地方债务风险（地方债务风险等级下降的省份数量等数据）。
   - 转移支付和增发国债对地方支出的支撑效果。
   - 财税体制改革对缓解土地财政依赖的长期意义和短期效果。
   - 各智库和学者对这些政策效果的评价（正面和负面）。

请在报告中明确标注每个政策的时间点、规模和来源（国务院文件、财政部公告、全国人大常委会决议、新华社、人民日报等官方发布），并引用中国社科院、中国人民大学等智库的评估观点。

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage contains the full text of the official Chinese government report on the execution of the 2024 central and local budgets and the draft budget for 2025, presented by the Ministry of Finance to the 14th National People's Congress (NPC) on March 5, 2025.

**2024 Budget Execution:**
- National general public budget revenue reached 219,702.12 billion yuan (98.1% of budget, up 1.3% from 2023). Tax revenue fell 3.4% (to 174,972.01 billion yuan) due to declining producer prices, while non-tax revenue rose 25.4%.
- National general public budget expenditure was 284,612.25 billion yuan (99.7% of budget, up 3.6%). The national deficit was 4,060 billion yuan.
- Central government deficit: 3,340 billion yuan; local deficit: 720 billion yuan.
- Government fund budget revenue fell 12.2% (to 62,090.4 billion yuan) mainly due to declining local land transfer income. 1 trillion yuan in ultra-long-term special treasury bonds were issued (700 billion for national strategies/security capacity, 300 billion for equipment renewal and consumer trade-ins).
- Social insurance fund revenue reached 118,944.7 billion yuan (up 5.2%); expenditure 106,061.28 billion yuan (up 7%), with year-end cumulative surplus of 143,372.3 billion yuan.
- NPC approved increasing the local government debt ceiling by 6 trillion yuan to replace hidden debt. Local governments' hidden debt total is set to drop from 14.3 trillion to 2.3 trillion yuan by end of 2028, saving about 600 billion yuan in interest.
- Defense spending in 2024: 1,665.21 billion yuan; education (central level): 166.07 billion yuan; science & technology: 361.91 billion yuan.

**2025 Budget Draft Highlights:**
- Deficit ratio set at ~4% (up 1 percentage point from 2024), with a deficit of 5,660 billion yuan (up 1,600 billion from 2024). Central deficit 4,860 billion; local 800 billion.
- National general public budget expenditure planned at 29,700.5 billion yuan (up 4.4%).
- New local government special bond quota: 4,400 billion yuan (up 500 billion). Ultra-long-term special treasury bonds: 1,300 billion yuan (800 billion for "two major" projects, 500 billion for "two new" policies).
- New special treasury bonds of 500 billion yuan to recapitalize large state-owned commercial banks.
- Central transfers to local governments: 10,341.5 billion yuan (same-caliber growth of 8.4%).
- Central defense budget 2025: 1,784.67 billion yuan (up 7.2%); education 174.44 billion (up 5%); science & technology 398.12 billion (up 10%).
- Support for consumption: 300 billion yuan ultra-long-term bonds for consumer trade-ins (up 150 billion); basic pension minimum raised 20 yuan/month per person; urban-rural resident medical insurance subsidy raised 30 yuan to 700 yuan/person/year.
- Fiscal policy focuses on five areas: raising deficit ratio, larger government bonds, optimizing expenditure structure, preventing risks, and increasing local transfers. Key reform measures include zero-based budgeting pilots, deepening fiscal and tax system reform, strengthening "three guarantees" (保) at the grassroots level, local debt risk prevention, and enhanced financial supervision.

The report also details 2025 plans for supporting domestic demand, modern industrial systems, science/education strategy, livelihood improvement, rural revitalization, new urbanization, regional coordination, ecological civilization, and national defense/foreign affairs.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 2: 国务院关于财政转移支付情况的报告-中国教育经济信息网 ---
URL: https://www.cee.edu.cn/n176/n564/n738/c650829/content.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage contains the full text of the State Council's Report on Fiscal Transfer Payments (国务院关于财政转移支付情况的报告), delivered by Finance Minister Liu Kun (刘昆) on August 28, 2023, at the 5th Session of the 14th National People's Congress Standing Committee. The report outlines China's fiscal transfer payment system and its reforms.

**Key points:**

1. **Basic framework**: China's fiscal transfer payment system was established in 1994 following the tax-sharing fiscal reform. It consists of "general transfer payments + special transfer payments," with general transfer payments (including co-financing of common fiscal powers) as the main body. In 2023, central-to-local transfer payments reached 10.06 trillion yuan.

2. **Management reforms (2014-2023)**:
   - Top-level design improvements (2016 reform of fiscal power and expenditure responsibility division)
   - Direct fund disbursement mechanism (established 2020 for COVID-19 response, regularized in 2021)
   - Regular evaluation mechanisms for transfer payments
   - Improved budget management and performance management (pre-performance assessments since 2022)

3. **Policy effectiveness**:
   - Reduced inter-regional fiscal disparities through special transfer payments for revolutionary base areas, ethnic regions, border areas, and underdeveloped regions
   - County-level basic fiscal support reward funds grew from 246.279 billion yuan (2018) to 410.7 billion yuan (2023), an average annual growth of 10.8%
   - Air pollution prevention funds grew from 20 billion yuan (2018) to 33 billion yuan (2023); water pollution prevention funds from 15 billion yuan to 25.7 billion yuan
   - Special poverty alleviation funds totaled 530.5 billion yuan over 2016-2020 (200 billion yuan annually added)
   - Industry foundation and manufacturing development funds totaled 40.249 billion yuan (2020-2023)
   - In 2023, 170 billion yuan in financial subsidy funds plus 30 billion yuan in carryover funds were allocated for COVID-19 prevention

4. **Future directions**:
   - Amend the Budget Law to make common fiscal power transfer payments a separate category; develop fiscal transfer payment regulations
   - Refine classification management of different transfer payment types
   - Improve budget compilation and optimize transfer payment project settings
   - Strengthen distribution, use, and performance management (general transfer payments to be issued within 30 days, special within 90 days after NPC budget approval)
   - Further reform sub-provincial (province-to-local) transfer payment systems
</summary>

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is the official report on China's 2025 central and local budget execution and the 2026 central and local budget draft, submitted by the Ministry of Finance to the 4th Session of the 14th National People's Congress on March 5, 2026, and published on March 16, 2026.

**2025 Budget Execution Highlights:**
- National general public budget revenue reached 21,604.488 billion yuan (98.3% of budget, down 1.7% from 2024); expenditures reached 28,739.542 billion yuan (96.8% of budget, up 1%), with a deficit of 5,660 billion yuan.
- Central government deficit was 4,860 billion yuan; local government deficit was 800 billion yuan.
- National government fund budget revenue was 5,770.355 billion yuan (down 7%); expenditure was 11,287.354 billion yuan (up 11.3%).
- National state-owned capital operating budget revenue was 854.695 billion yuan (up 25.8%); expenditure was 264.731 billion yuan (down 15.1%).
- National social insurance fund revenue was 12,603.368 billion yuan (up 4.9%); expenditure was 11,141.41 billion yuan (up 5.4%), with year-end accumulated surplus of 15,956.253 billion yuan.
- National defense spending reached 1,784.665 billion yuan (100% of budget); science and technology spending was 387.705 billion yuan.
- Issued 1.3 trillion yuan in ultra-long-term special treasury bonds (800 billion for "two heavy" construction, 500 billion for "two new" policies), 4.4 trillion yuan in new local special bonds, and 500 billion yuan in special treasury bonds for major state-owned commercial banks' capital replenishment.
- 2 trillion yuan in local government bonds fully issued to replace existing hidden debt, lowering average debt interest costs by over 2.5 percentage points.
- National fiscal science spending over the "14th Five-Year Plan" period totaled 5.4 trillion yuan (average annual growth of 5.7%); national fiscal education spending kept above 4% of GDP.
- 12.67 million new urban jobs created in 2025.
- Childcare subsidy of 3,600 yuan per child per year for children under 3, benefiting over 30 million infants.
- Basic pension for urban and rural residents raised by 20 yuan per month minimum; retirees' basic pension adjusted by 2%.
- End of 2025: national debt balance was 41,231.768 billion yuan; local government debt balance was 54,823.082 billion yuan.

**2026 Budget Draft Highlights:**
- National general public budget expenditure planned at 30,010 billion yuan (up 4.4%), with deficit ratio around 4% (deficit of 5,890 billion yuan, up 230 billion yuan).
- Central deficit: 5,090 billion yuan (up 230 billion); local deficit: 800 billion yuan (unchanged).
- Continue issuing 1.3 trillion yuan ultra-long-term special treasury bonds; issue 300 billion yuan special treasury bonds for bank capital replenishment; 4.4 trillion yuan new local special bonds.
- Central transfers to local governments: 10,415 billion yuan (up 2.2%).
- Central science and technology expenditure: 426.42 billion yuan (up 10%); basic research up 16.3%.
- Central defense expenditure: 1,909.561 billion yuan (up 7%).
- Central education expenditure: 192.476 billion yuan (up 5%).
- 100 billion yuan special fund for fiscal-financial coordination to boost domestic demand.
- 250 billion yuan ultra-long-term special treasury bonds for consumer trade-in programs; 800 billion yuan for "two heavy" construction; 200 billion yuan for large-scale equipment renewal.
- Central budget investment: 755 billion yuan (up 20 billion yuan).
- Rural revitalization support funds: 177 billion yuan.
- New urban residents' citizenization incentive: 42 billion yuan.
- Key ecological functional zone transfers: 122.9 billion yuan (up 2%).
- 2026 is the opening year of the "15th Five-Year Plan" (2026-2030).

**Key 2026 Policy Directions:**
- Continue more proactive fiscal policy with five aspects: expanding expenditure scale, optimizing government bond tools, improving transfer payment efficiency, optimizing expenditure structure, and strengthening fiscal-financial coordination.
- Support building a strong domestic market, cultivating new growth drivers, accelerating high-level technological self-reliance, improving people's livelihoods (employment, education, healthcare, social security), rural revitalization, new urbanization, green transformation, and national defense/foreign affairs.
- Deepen fiscal and tax reforms including zero-based budgeting expansion, local tax system development, consumption tax adjustments, and individual income tax improvements.
- Strengthen local government debt management with zero tolerance for new hidden debt and promoting financing platform transformation.
- Maintain "three guarantees" (basic livelihood, wages, and government operations) at the grassroots level.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"2026年继续实施更加积极的财政政策。'更加积极'既体现在扩大资金规模上，更体现在提高资金使用效益上。全国一般公共预算支出规模达到300100亿元，比上年增长4.4%。赤字率按照4%左右安排，全国财政赤字规模58900亿元、比上年增加2300亿元。"

<summary>
This is the official report on the Execution of the 2025 Central and Local Budgets and the Draft 2026 Central and Local Budgets, published by Xinhua News Agency on March 14, 2026, and presented via People's Daily (人民网) as part of the 2026 National Two Sessions (全国两会) coverage.

**Part I: 2025 Budget Execution**

**Central General Public Budget:**

2. Foster new growth drivers (support new quality productive forces, AI+, 6G, quantum technology, embodied intelligence)
3. Accelerate high-level technological self-reliance (central science & technology spending up 10%; basic research up 16.3%)

<summary>
This webpage is from the Fujian Provincial Department of Finance (福建省财政厅) website and contains a republished Xinhua News article titled "新华解码丨透视我国增发2023年国债1万亿元的深意" (Xinhua Decoding: Insights into China's Additional Issuance of 1 Trillion Yuan in 2023 Government Bonds), dated October 25, 2023.

The key details include:

**Why the bonds were issued:** To support post-disaster recovery and reconstruction and enhance disaster prevention, mitigation, and relief capabilities. Multiple regions in China suffered severe damage from rainstorms, floods, and typhoons in 2023, and existing budgeted disaster relief funds were insufficient.

**How the funds will be used:** The 1 trillion yuan will be issued in Q4 2023 and allocated entirely to local governments through transfer payments. Of this, 500 billion yuan will be used this year and 500 billion yuan carried over to next year. Funds will be directed to eight priority areas: post-disaster recovery and reconstruction, key flood control projects, natural disaster emergency response capacity enhancement, other key flood control projects, irrigation district construction and soil erosion control, urban drainage and flood prevention improvements, comprehensive natural disaster prevention systems, and high-standard farmland construction in the Northeast and Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei disaster-affected regions.

**Budget and deficit adjustments:** Central local transfer payments will increase by 500 billion yuan; local general public budget expenditures increase by 500 billion yuan (expenditure growth rate rises from 5.2% to 7.4%). The 2023 national fiscal deficit rises from 3.88 trillion yuan to 4.88 trillion yuan; the central fiscal deficit increases from 3.16 trillion yuan to 4.16 trillion yuan. The deficit ratio is expected to rise from 3% to approximately 3.8%.

**Management of funds:** The bond funds will be included in the direct allocation mechanism (直达机制) for full-process tracking and monitoring. The Ministry of Finance will establish normalized supervision mechanisms through its regional bureaus to prevent misappropriation and diversion of bond funds.

Expert commentary is included from Liu Yi (刘怡), Director of the Finance Department at Peking University's School of Economics, and Shi Yinghua (石英华), a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Fiscal Sciences, both noting the necessity, fiscal prudence, and policy continuity of the measure.

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a news article from 财联社 (Cailian Press) published on June 25, 2025, reporting on China's local government bond issuance trends. Key findings include:

1. **Overall issuance**: As of June 24, local government bonds had a net issuance of 2.48 trillion yuan this year, a sharp decrease of 4.31 trillion yuan compared to the same period last year.

2. **Special refinancing bonds**: The front-loading of special refinancing bonds (for replacing hidden debt) reached 90% of the annual 2 trillion yuan quota. Total special refinancing bonds issued reached 2.88 trillion yuan by June 24, significantly higher than last year's ~1.66 trillion yuan, comprising 727.279 billion yuan in general refinancing bonds and 2.15 trillion yuan in special refinancing bonds.

3. **Reasons for slower new bond issuance**: CITIC Fixed Income team noted that Q1 issuance was concentrated on debt reduction (化债), crowding out new bond issuance windows, and project starts were limited under the debt risk prevention framework.

4. **New special bonds slow**: Special new special bonds (特殊新增专项债) have been slow this year, with only 410.538 billion yuan issued so far, though June saw 168.13 billion yuan issued. Hebei, Sichuan, and Hubei provinces issued such bonds at quarter-end. Land reserve funding through new special bonds has only reached 169.9 billion yuan.

5. **Q3 outlook**: CITIC Fixed Income estimates Q3 new special bond issuance could approach 2 trillion yuan, as the traditional peak season for new special bonds arrives after the debt-swap special refinancing bond work concludes.

6. **"Self-review self-issuance" (自审自发)**: Guangdong issued a work plan on June 24 to advance the "self-review and self-issuance" mechanism for special bonds. Four provinces (Hunan, Guangdong, Fujian, Sichuan) have now issued such documents, with their new special bond issuance progress currently low (Hunan 13.8 billion yuan, Guangdong 7.85 billion yuan, Fujian 7.6 billion yuan, Sichuan 17.175 billion yuan).

The article cites analysts including 李晗 (Li Han) from CITIC Fixed Income, 徐琳 (Xu Lin) from 兴证固收 (Xingzheng Fixed Income), and 胡恒松 (Hu Hengsong), deputy general manager of 财达证券 (Caida Securities).
</summary>

--- SOURCE 2: A股-研报详情 ---
URL: https://stock.finance.sina.com.cn/stock/view/paper.php?symbol=sh000001&reportid=788730419410

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a fixed-income research report by Yang Yewei and Wang Chunyi of Guosheng Securities (published 2024-12-28) titled "化债大年 地方债的七大新特征" (Seven New Characteristics of Local Government Bonds in a Major Debt-Restructuring Year). The report analyzes seven key features of local government bond issuance in 2024 amid China's large-scale implicit debt resolution efforts:

1. **Debt-restructuring bond issuance surged**: 800 billion yuan new special bonds + 400 billion yuan surplus quota + 2 trillion yuan refinancing special bonds were allocated for debt resolution. The 2024 quota of 2 trillion yuan was fully issued by year-end.

2. **Quota allocation shifted**: 2024 allocations depended more on implicit debt scale and fiscal capacity, while 2023 favored key/priority regions. Non-key regions saw significantly increased quotas (key regions accounted for 32% of 2024 allocations vs. 70% of special refinancing quota in 2023).

3. **Slower issuance pace**: In H1 2024, only 38% of new special bonds were issued (vs. 85% in 2022 and 58% in 2023 at the same period), due to delayed project application cycles (~1 quarter lag) and stricter project review. Issuance accelerated in Q3.

4. **Longer maturities**: Weighted average maturity of local bonds lengthened from 12.39 years (2023) to 14.43 years (2024). Special refinancing bond maturities stretched dramatically from 8.56 to 17.60 years, with 88% of the 2 trillion debt-restructuring bonds having maturities of 10+ years (30% at 30 years).

5. **Narrower issuance spreads and lower costs**: Average issuance spread fell from 14.3bp (2023) to 8.4bp (2024). Unlike in late 2023 when spreads widened above 20bp, the 2024 surge in debt-restructuring bond issuance kept average spreads within 10bp.

6. **Regional spread divergence**: Less-developed regions (Yunnan, Guizhou, Xinjiang, Qinghai) saw spreads above 10bp, while developed regions (Fujian, Zhejiang, Ningbo) saw 4-5bp. "Failed" issuances (spreads ≥15bp) concentrated in Henan, Guizhou, Jiangxi, Inner Mongolia, and Xinjiang.

7. **Increased trading volume and turnover**: 2024 (Jan-Nov) local bond trading reached 17.2 trillion yuan, up 29.4% year-over-year, with turnover rising from 35% to 40%. Hunan, Shandong, Tianjin, and Chongqing had turnover rates above 50%.

**2025 Outlook**: New general bond quota expected to remain around 720 billion yuan; new special bond quota projected at 4.6 trillion yuan (3.8 trillion base + 800 billion for debt restructuring). Total issuance estimated at ~10.0 trillion yuan with net financing of 6.9 trillion yuan (slightly up from 2024's 9.7 trillion issued / 6.8 trillion net). The State Council's recent policy (《关于优化完善地方政府专项债券管理机制的意见》) launched a pilot "self-review and self-issuance" program in 15 regions (accounting for 52-58% of new special bonds issued 2020-2024), expanding investment fields and capital usage ratios, which could accelerate issuance. However, 2.3 trillion yuan of special bond funds remained unused as of October 2024, and local matching capacity and debt constraints may temper the pace.

**Risk warnings**: Policy changes exceeding expectations, statistical measurement errors, and higher-than-expected local bond supply.
</summary>

"2024年化债额度分配或主要取决于各地隐债规模及财力情况，而2023年对重点地区倾斜较多" (2024 debt-resolution quota allocation mainly depended on implicit debt scale and fiscal capacity, while 2023 favored key regions more)

URL: https://www.yicai.com/news/103109692.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a news article from 第一财经 (Yicai), published on March 30, 2026, reporting on the accelerated pace of local government debt resolution (化债) in China and the rapid reduction of hidden debt balances.

Key facts and data points:
- As of March 30, 2026, local governments have issued approximately 0.96 trillion yuan in refinancing special bonds to replace hidden debt, accounting for nearly half of the planned 2 trillion yuan issuance for the year.
- Under the central government's debt resolution package, local governments will issue 2 trillion yuan in refinancing special bonds and 0.8 trillion yuan in new special bonds this year to replace existing hidden debt, extend maturities, and reduce interest costs.
- According to Ministry of Finance data, the national hidden local government debt balance stood at 14.3 trillion yuan at end-2023, falling to 10.5 trillion yuan by end-2024.
- Economist Luo Zhiheng (粤开证券首席经济学家) estimates that ~3.1 trillion yuan in various local government bonds were issued in 2025 to replace hidden debt, which should reduce the hidden debt balance to 7.4 trillion yuan by end-2025.
- After the full issuance of the 2 trillion yuan replacement bonds in 2025, average debt interest costs across regions fell by more than 2.5 percentage points. The Ministry of Finance estimates the five-year (2024-2028) debt resolution plan could save approximately 600 billion yuan in cumulative interest expenses.
- Guangxi's 2025 budget report shows local issuance of special bonds for hidden debt replacement saves over 1 billion yuan in annual interest.
- The average remaining maturity of national local government bonds reached 10.5 years in 2025, with replacement special bonds averaging 19.8 years in issuance terms.
- By end-2025, over 82% of local government financing platforms (LGFVs) had exited, and outstanding operating financial debt of financing platforms fell by more than 74%.
- As of end-2025, total local government debt stood at approximately 54.82 trillion yuan, within the limit approved by the National People's Congress.

The article also discusses: financing platform transformation into ordinary state-owned enterprises, the distinction between hidden debt and operating debt of LGFVs, the six dimensions of progress in 2025 (hidden debt resolution, debt cost reduction, operating debt management, arrears clearance, platform transformation, and long-term mechanism construction), and the overall assessment that local debt risk remains safe and controllable with management shifting from emergency response to routine regulation.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 4: 2024年三路化债资金3.38万亿元，2025年有哪些化债新思路？ - 21经济网 ---
URL: https://www.21jingji.com/article/20250122/herald/39a722cebc73fa7683315487d84d0ab8.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
## 2024年地方化债工作总结与2025年化债新思路（21世纪经济报道，2025年1月22日）

**核心主题：** 本文由21世纪经济报道记者周潇枭报道，总结2024年地方化债工作的执行情况，并展望2025年的化债政策与工作重点。

### 2024年化债资金落地情况
2024年是地方化债的大年。机构统计显示，2024年全年三路化债资金共计约**3.38万亿元**，是近年来化债力度最大的一次。具体构成包括：
- **"特殊"再融资债券**：5018亿元，用于偿还存量债务
- **"特殊"新增专项债券**：8778亿元，用于化解存量政府投资项目债务（占全部新增专项债比重21.9%）
- **置换存量隐性债务的再融资专项债券**：2万亿元，于2024年四季度仅1个月时间（11月18日河南首发至12月18日北京收官）密集落地

### 置换债券各省配额
主要省份获得的2万亿元置换债券额度（2024~2026年三年平均分配）：
- 江苏：2511亿元/年（三年合计7533亿元）
- 湖南：1288亿元
- 河南：1227亿元
- 贵州：1176亿元
- 四川：1148亿元（三年合计3444亿元）
- 山东（不含青岛）：1113亿元
- 湖北：982亿元、安徽：980亿元、云南：878亿元、天津：771亿元、重庆：771亿元、辽宁（不含大连）：667亿元

财政部部长蓝佛安表示，6万亿元地方政府债务限额由国务院一次性提请全国人大常委会审议批准，分三年安排实施，全部安排为专项债务限额，允许地方用于置换纳入监测范围的各类隐性债务。

### 盘活4000亿元结存限额
2024年从地方债务结存限额中安排4000亿元，用以补充地方政府综合财力。这是继2022年（当时为稳增长动用5000亿元）之后再次动用结存限额。财政部在分配时在不同省份间进行调剂，部分省份（如江苏、四川、贵州）将其全部用于偿还存量债务、置换存量隐性债务，而北京、浙江等则全部用于扩投资、稳增长。

### 2025年展望
1. **化债资金继续落地**：2025年仍有**2.8万亿元**地方债券用于化债（2万亿元置换再融资专项债 + 8000万元新增专项债用于化债）。
2. **各省置换债券配额或与2024年相当**：江苏、四川等省份预算调整方案显示2025~2026年额度与2024年相同。
3. **2025年发行速度预计加快**：截至2025年1月22日，已有8个省份/单列市（青岛、湖北、天津、海南、河南、北京、山东、厦门）披露化债债券发行计划，合计约1719亿元。中央财经大学教授温来成预计2025年上半年发债速度将明显快于2024年。
4. **债务风险仍存**：地方隐性债务形式多样（如部分存量PPP项目可能带来新增隐性债务），北京、广东此前已宣布隐性债务清零，但2024年底北京仍发行了47亿元再融资专项债用于置换存量隐性债务、201亿元"特殊"再融资债券用于偿还存量债务；广东2024年10月也发行了约169亿元"特殊"再融资债券。
5. **专家建议**：中国社科院何代欣建议落实化债资金、适当拓宽债务置换和风险覆盖范围、通过盘活存量资产减轻债务压力；温来成预计2025年地方新增专项债规模将突破4万亿元，需注重提高专项债项目质量，避免将债券资金投入没有还本付息能力的项目。

### 专家观点
- **何代欣（中国社科院财政研究室主任）**：2024年中央和地方多渠道找钱，既化解债务、防范风险，又通过增加债券发行带动地方投资。
- **温来成（中央财经大学教授）**：以往每年城投债还本付息规模约3万亿元，近三年财政部每年安排2.8万亿元化债资金，应能较好缓解地方隐性债务压力。
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"2024年无疑已经是地方化债的大年……2024年四季度仅1个月的时间，就落地了2万亿元置换债券用于化解隐性债务。"、"财政部部长蓝佛安表示，国务院一次性向全国人大常委会提请审议批准增加6万亿元地方政府债务限额，分三年安排实施……6万亿元全部安排为专项债务限额，允许地方用于置换纳入监测范围的各类隐性债务。"、"中信证券固收团队统计数据显示，2024年债务化解方式更为多元化，全年累计发行化债资金3.38万亿元。"、"中国社科院财经战略研究院财政研究室主任何代欣表示，2024年中央和地方确实在多渠道找钱，一方面要化解债务、防范风险，确保地方稳健运行；另一方面财政政策要积极作为，通过增加债券发行来带动地方投资。"、"中央财经大学教授温来成对21世纪经济报道记者表示，2025年地方行动比较快，预计2025年上半年发债速度会明显快于2024年。因为以往年份每年城投债还本付息规模在3万亿元左右，近三年财政部每年安排2.8万亿元化债资金，应该能比较好地缓解地方隐性债务压力。"
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 5: NIFD 官方网站 ---
URL: http://www.nifd.cn/SeriesReport/Details/4814

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a financial risk weekly report (Debt Observation Weekly Report 2025 Issue 47, dated December 1, 2025) published by NIFD (National Institution for Finance & Development). The report covers four major debt-related developments in China and two expert opinion pieces.

**Debt Dynamics Section:**

1. **500 billion yuan local government bond quota acceleration** - The Ministry of Finance announced on October 17 that 500 billion yuan of local government debt balance quota would be distributed, with 300 billion yuan for debt resolution and 200 billion yuan for stabilizing investment. In the first 11 months of 2025, ~3.5 trillion yuan was used for resolving hidden debt, arrears to enterprises, and legacy PPP projects, while over 3.9 trillion yuan went to new general and special bonds for investment expansion. Special refinancing bonds resumed issuance in August after no issuance from January-July (2.8 trillion yuan pre-arranged), with monthly issuance of 3.3 billion (Aug), 6.2 billion (Sep), 45 billion (Oct), and 176.7 billion (Nov) yuan. November saw 492.2 billion yuan in new special bonds. Infrastructure investment fell 0.1% YoY in Jan-Oct 2025. He Daixin (Chinese Academy of Social Sciences) noted the additional 300 billion yuan in Q4 supports the "proactive and steady resolution of local government debt risks."

2. **Special bonds turning into patient capital for tech investment** - Over 800 billion yuan in local government special bonds has been directed toward government investment funds across Guangdong, Sichuan, Shanghai, Beijing, Jiangsu, Guangzhou, Zhejiang and other regions. On November 28, Guangdong, Sichuan and Shanghai jointly issued 20 billion yuan in special bonds for government funds. This marks a policy shift since December 2024 when a "negative list" management approach was adopted, removing the pre-2019 restriction that special bonds could not fund equity/industry investment funds. This shift responds to local fiscal revenue pressure and the need to support technological innovation.

3. **Multiple regions preparing 2026 special bond project reserves** - The Ministry of Finance will continue early issuance of 2026 new local government debt quotas. Regions like Hubei Tianmen have held planning meetings for 2026 projects focusing on education, healthcare, transportation and ecological environment. Professor Bai Yanfeng (Central University of Finance and Economics) emphasized early planning is essential for longer-cycle projects, particularly for old community renovation and urban renewal. 2025 special bond issuance has been characterized as "fast pace, optimal structure, good results."

--- SOURCE 8: 何为特殊再融资债券？此次重启对地方政府化债有多大作用？|界面新闻 ---
URL: https://www.jiemian.com/article/10236940.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article, authored by 罗志恒 (Luo Zhiheng), Chief Economist at 粤开证券 (Yuekai Securities), published on October 17, 2023, by 界面新闻 (Jiemian News), analyzes China's special refinancing bonds (特殊再融资债券) and their role in local government debt resolution.

**What are special refinancing bonds:**
- Regular refinancing bonds (再融资债券) have been issued since April 2018 to repay maturing local government bonds. They are used for "borrowing new to repay old," do not increase debt balances, and must correspond one-to-one with maturing bonds. Issuance volumes from 2018-2022 were 6,817, 11,484, 18,913, 31,189, and 26,110 billion yuan respectively.
- Special refinancing bonds began in December 2020, when Jiangsu first issued bonds with funds designated for "repaying principal of stock debts included in government debt management" rather than disclosing specific bonds being repaid. These are mainly used to swap out implicit (hidden) debt, increase explicit local government debt balances, and are limited by regional debt caps.
- Two historical issuance peaks: Round 1 (Dec 2020–Sep 2021) totaled 627.8 billion yuan for county-level implicit debt resolution pilots (led by Chongqing, Tianjin, Jiangsu, Xinjiang, Guizhou); Round 2 (Oct 2021–Jun 2022) totaled 504.18 billion yuan for full-area no-implicit-debt pilots, concentrated in developed regions (Beijing 325.23b, Guangdong 113.48b, Shanghai 65.48b).

**The third round restart (October 2023):**
- Inner Mongolia's issuance of 66.32 billion yuan on October 9, 2023 marked the start of Round 3, initially described as repaying government arrears to enterprises, then adjusted to "repaying stock debts."
- Driven by the Politburo's July 24, 2023 call for a "package of debt resolution measures" and the State Council's September 20, 2023 approval of the "Action Plan for Clearing Arrears Owed to Enterprises."
- As of October 14, 2023, 17 provinces/cities disclosed plans totaling 726.3 billion yuan. Tier 1: Yunnan (107.6b) and Inner Mongolia (106.7b); Tier 2: Guizhou (88.24b), Liaoning (87.04b), Hunan (64.34b); Tier 3: Guangxi, Chongqing; Tier 4: Fujian, Shandong, Jilin, Gansu, Tianjin, Jiangxi, Dalian (10-30b each); Tier 5: Qinghai (9.6b), Hubei (9.2b), Ningxia (8b).
- Notable: Inner Mongolia's issuance exceeded its theoretical cap of 63.95 billion yuan (based on its 933.97b debt balance vs. 997.92b limit), suggesting cross-provincial reallocation of unused debt quotas.
- Three differences from prior rounds: (1) larger scale (726.3b vs. 627.8b and 504.18b); (2) faster pace (10 working days vs. 10 and 9 months); (3) dominated by general bonds (79.4% general vs. 20.6% special, versus 54.0% and 23.8% in earlier rounds).

**Limitations — "treats symptoms, not root causes":**
- Theoretical issuance ceiling is 2.6 trillion yuan (national debt limit of 37.6t minus balance of 35.1t), only 4.7% of the 55 trillion yuan in outstanding city investment platform (城投) interest-bearing debt.
- Unused quota space is unevenly distributed, concentrated in Shanghai (276.55b), Jiangsu (190.01b), and Beijing (163.71b), with minimal space in Tibet, Heilongjiang, Hunan, Chongqing, and Qinghai.

**Short-term resolution measures proposed:**
1. Strict audits to distinguish government debt from enterprise debt; differentiate debt from public services vs. distorted political performance.
2. Fiscal resolution: use fiscal funds, sell government equity/land/state assets (e.g., Guizhou's "Moutai debt resolution"), use project carryover funds, and optimize debt structure via swaps.
3. Financial-fiscal coordination: negotiate extensions with banks (e.g., Guizhou's Zunyi Daoqiao restructuring of 15.594 billion yuan loans into 20-year terms at 3%-4.5% rates), bankruptcy restructuring for risk isolation, asset management companies purchasing city investment bonds, and policy bank medium/long-term loans.
4. Adhere to "whose child is held by whom" and "no central bailout" principles, but set conditions for central government rescue based on risk severity and asset externalities, with accountability to avoid moral hazard.
5. Reallocate debt quotas—increase short-term quotas for underdeveloped regions to make room for explicit debt, but in the long run link quotas to economic development, borrowing capacity, and expenditure responsibilities.

**Long-term institutional reforms (nine measures):**
1. Clarify government-market boundaries and limit government functions/expenditure responsibilities.
2. Establish performance assessment and fiscal evaluation systems under multi-objective governance.
3. Create pre-policy evaluation and post-implementation accountability mechanisms to prevent fiscal risk contamination.
4. Stabilize macro tax burden; shift from quantity-based to efficiency-based tax cuts; consider structural tax increases (consumption tax, environmental tax, resource tax) and explore "data finance."
5. Accelerate central-local fiscal reform; devolve consumption tax to localities; move expenditure responsibilities upward to central/provincial levels.
6. Issue long-term construction treasury bonds for national/cross-regional infrastructure; gradually reduce special bond use; establish a three-track system of long-term treasury bonds, local general bonds, and local special bonds.
7. Optimize regional debt structure; moderately relax borrowing quotas for metropolitan areas and population-inflow regions; strengthen performance management linking assets and liabilities.
8. Transform city investment platforms into ordinary operating state-owned enterprises by stripping their government financing functions.
9. Strengthen fiscal-financial coordination, with fiscal policy as the lead and monetary/financial environment supporting it.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"特殊再融资债券化债治标不治本，必须通过体制机制的联动改革抑制隐性债务产生的土壤。" (Special refinancing bond debt resolution treats symptoms but not root causes; institutional reform is necessary to suppress the soil that breeds implicit debt.)
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 10: 特殊再融资债券 ---
URL: https://baike.baidu.com/item/%E7%89%B9%E6%AE%8A%E5%86%8D%E8%9E%8D%E8%B5%84%E5%80%BA%E5%88%B8/67773345

SUMMARY:
<summary>
特殊再融资债券是地方政府为置换存量隐性债务而发行的一种债券，属于地方政府债券和再融资债券的特殊品种。其区别于普通再融资债券的关键在于募集资金用途明确为"偿还存量债务"，而非"偿还到期地方政府债券本金"。该债券的核心目的是将高成本、不透明的隐性债务转化为低成本、透明的显性债务，实现地方政府债务的显性化和借新还旧，本质上是"一揽子化债方案"中的重要工具。

【发展历程】
- 第一轮发行（2020年12月至2021年9月）：用于"建制县隐性债务化解试点"，累计发行规模约6278亿元（另一说法为6128亿元）。
- 第二轮发行（2021年10月至2022年6月）：用于北京、上海、广东三地的"全域无隐性债务"试点，合计发行约5042亿元。
- 2023年9月起，作为"一揽子化债方案"的第一步重启发行，截至2023年底累计发行规模超过1.3万亿元（约1.39万亿元），发行规模大、节奏快。发行地区向贵州、云南、内蒙古、辽宁、天津等债务压力较大的中西部和东北地区倾斜。
- 2024年继续发行以支持隐性债务化解，全国人大批准增加6万亿元置换债额度。
- 2025年，用于解决政府拖欠款的特殊再融资债券预计规模超过2500亿元。

【制度内容与特点】
- 发行主体为地方政府，由地方政府承担还本付息责任。
- 募集资金用于置换地方政府存量隐性债务、偿还政府拖欠企业账款等。
- 发行额度主要来源于地方政府债务结存限额（即债务限额与余额的差额），特殊时期可通过全国人大批准新增额度。
- 债券期限以3年、5年、7年、10年等中长期品种为主，自第三轮发行起出现30年期超长期品种。
- 债券类型包括一般债券和专项债券，2023年重启后的发行以一般债券为主。
- 特点：短期见效快、实施难度相对较小、有利于债务透明化，但发行规模受区域债务限额约束。

【与其他债券的比较】
- 普通再融资债券资金用途为"偿还到期地方政府债券本金"，与到期债券一一对应；特殊再融资债券用途范围更广，主要用于置换隐性债务。
- 特殊再融资债券已逐步取代早期的置换债券，成为地方政府化解隐性债务的主要工具。
- 新增专项债券募集资金用于新的公益性项目资本支出，而特殊再融资债券不用于新项目建设，专门用于化解存量债务，实现债务显性化、期限拉长和成本降低。
</summary>

<key_excerpts>

</key_excerpts>

- The article, authored by 程思炜 (Cheng Siwei) and edited by 于海荣 (Yu Hairong), focuses on the fiscal and tax reform provisions in the "Decision of the Central Committee on Further Deepening Reform Comprehensively and Advancing Chinese Modernization."

<summary>
This is a research report published on Sina Finance (2024-06-24) from China Galaxy Securities (中国银河证券) titled "The Strategic Implications of Consumption Tax Reform — Series on Third Plenum Reform Outlook" (消费税改革的战略深意——三中全会改革前瞻系列). The report analyzes the upcoming consumption tax reform in China, which is expected to enter a pilot phase in 2024 and is a key focus of the Third Plenum fiscal and tax system reform.

KEY CONTENT:

**Background:** The 2019 State Council document (国发〔2019〕21号) explicitly proposed "postponing the consumption tax collection stage and steadily devolving it to local governments." The 2024 fiscal budget draft called for "planning consumption tax reform and improving VAT system." Unlike VAT (which will likely complete legislation this year), consumption tax has been in preparatory review for three consecutive years without entering the legislative plan, suggesting "reform first, legislation later."

**What "下划" (downward transfer) and "后移" (backward shifting) mean:**
- Consumption tax is currently a central government tax fully collected at the production stage
- "下划" = allocating part of consumption tax revenue to local governments
- "后移" = shifting collection from production to wholesale/retail stage, meaning tax goes to consuming regions rather than producing regions

**Current consumption tax structure (2023):**
- Total revenue: 1.61 trillion yuan, 8.9% of total tax revenue
- Composition: tobacco 53.4%, petroleum fuels 33%, automobiles 7%, alcohol 4.6% (these four account for 98%)
- Regional share under current system: East 39.9%, West 28.5%, Central 16.8%, Northeast 7.8%

**Four impact dimensions:**
1. **Total level - supplementing local finances:** If all tax items shift collection and 50% is devolved to local governments, East/Central/West/Northeast regions would gain 330.8B, 156B, 159.3B, and 50B yuan respectively. Eastern provinces have larger absolute gains due to higher consumption (49.4% of national tobacco/alcohol spending, 42.8% of refined oil, 51.1% of autos).

2. **Regional level - redistribution of local finances:** Marginal fiscal growth rates (incremental consumption tax/local fiscal revenue) would be East 5.2%, Central 7.8%, West 7.3%, Northeast 9.6%. Northeast and Central/West regions benefit more relatively due to lower revenue bases. Provinces like Heilongjiang, Liaoning, and Hubei see the largest improvement.

3. **Supply-demand level - guiding better consumption environments:** Shifting from "production-place principle" to "consumption-place principle" would encourage local governments to strengthen consumption infrastructure and promote consumption, addressing the "heavy production, light consumption" orientation that has caused supply-demand imbalance. Producing provinces (Shanghai, Guizhou, Yunnan, Hubei, Hunan) would see negative tax growth, while consuming provinces (Guangdong, Shandong, Henan, Zhejiang) would see positive growth.

4. **Industry level - potential "Matthew effect" (马太效应) in competition:** Since consumption tax is a price-inclusive tax, shifting collection from production to retail raises the tax base from factory price to retail price, increasing terminal prices. Low price-elasticity monopolistic enterprises (e.g., tobacco) can shift tax burden; high-elasticity products (liquor, autos) may need to cut prices, intensifying competitive "Matthew effect" and compressing profits for weaker firms.

**Future reform pathway:** Of the 15 consumption tax items, 12 already have controllable collection capabilities at the retail stage (tobacco, fireworks, motorcycles, small cars, high-end cosmetics, jewelry, luxury watches, yachts, solid wood flooring, golf equipment, refined oil, alcohol). Only disposable chopsticks, batteries, and coatings lack systematic collection mechanisms. The expected path: pilot with small tax items (like high-end cosmetics, jewelry) first, then expand to tobacco, oil, and autos; initially devolve only incremental revenue, then gradually raise the central-local split ratio; eventually expand the tax base to adjust supply-demand.

**Risks:** Policy implementation falling short of expectations; estimation method errors; domestic economic recovery weaker than expected.

Report details: Published June 23, 2024 by analyst Zhang Di (张迪, S0130524060001) with research assistant Nie Tianqi (聂天奇).

   - Need to reserve space for future rural housing and land reform

The report concludes that the tax is unlikely to be implemented in the short term, and its immediate impact on the market would be minimal, but it represents an important long-term reform. Related news items from November 2016 indicate that individual income tax and real estate tax reforms were still being actively promoted, with direct taxes becoming a key breakthrough area for tax reform.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 1: 地方化债“成绩单”揭晓，“下降”成关键词，凸显在五大方面 ---
URL: https://m.cls.cn/detail/1601159

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a news article from 财联社 (Cailian Press) dated February 23, 2024, reporting on the 2023 local government debt resolution ("化债") achievements across China, based on a review of 2024 government work reports from 31 provinces and 86 cities/counties, combined with 2023 budget execution drafts and 2024 budget drafts.

**2023 Key Achievements (Five Main Trends):**
1. **Debt risk level downgrades**: The Ministry of Finance classifies local debt risk into four tiers (Red ≥300% debt ratio, Orange 200-300%, Yellow 120-200%, Green <120%). Examples: Inner Mongolia's Alxa and Wuhai cities and 8 banner/county governments exited Orange; Baotou exited Red; Hubei Huanggang and Inner Mongolia's Zhuozi County exited Orange; Jiangsu province maintained Green; Yancheng turned Green; Liaoning's Nanfen District moved from Yellow to Green for the first time.

2. **Debt scale and debt ratio declines**: Ningxia achieved "three declines" (debt scale, debt ratio, risk level) with record resolution efforts; Guangxi saw significant reduction in implicit debt; Gansu resolved 104.84 billion yuan of financing platform debt. According to Guangfa Fixed Income chief Liu Yu, 23 provinces saw slower growth in interest-bearing debt of bond-issuing city investment companies by Q3 2023. Jilin, Tibet and Guizhou saw declines exceeding 50 percentage points; Yunnan, Chongqing and Gansu saw declines of 40-50 percentage points. Financing costs also fell—Changde, Hunan lowered average annual interest rates on existing debt to ~5%, Xiangtan to below 4%.

3. **Special refinancing bonds**: From September 2023, a new round of special refinancing bonds was issued, totaling nearly 1.4 trillion yuan. In Q4, the National People's Congress Standing Committee approved 1 trillion yuan in additional national bonds managed as special bonds. Xiangtan, Hunan secured 65.09 billion yuan—the largest amount among prefecture-level cities disclosed. Other recipients included Zhuzhou's Lukou District (3.194 billion yuan total across multiple bond types), Bazhong, Sichuan (1.8 billion yuan), Jiang'an County, Yibin (2.4 billion yuan, top in the province among counties), and Tonghai County, Yunnan (432 million yuan).

4. **Implicit debt resolution pilots**: Multiple cities/counties obtained implicit debt resolution pilot status, including Loudi, Hunan (city level and Lengshuijiang City approved as national pilots), Gaogang District in Taizhou, Jiangsu, and Anyue County in Ziyang, Sichuan.

5. **Reduction in financing platform numbers**: Henan pushed to strip government financing functions from platforms with orderly reductions; Chongqing's Fuling District reduced 19 state-owned enterprises with 7 platform SOEs clearing implicit debt; Nanjing's Qinhuai District reduced platform numbers by 15.

**2024 Plans:**
- Focus on "implementing" debt resolution measures: strengthening risk monitoring, implementing financial support for debt resolution, and promoting platform transformation.
- Jiangxi and Yunnan will use "one debt, one strategy" approaches; Fujian, Shaanxi and Henan will target high-risk regions; Jilin will optimize debt structure and reduce costs.
- Henan will strengthen risk monitoring and early warning; Ningxia and Sichuan will push for merged supervision of implicit and statutory debt; Xiangtan will build a full-coverage, penetrating supervision system.
- Financial support emphasized: Changde will push for full implicit debt swap; Loudi will implement the "ten measures" including big bank takeover and non-standard debt swaps; Weifang, Shandong secured 430 billion yuan in new financing support over 5 years and activated 10.37 billion yuan in six types of asset resources.
- More provinces (Guizhou, Tianjin, Jilin, Sichuan, Shaanxi, Hubei, Zhejiang) will seek central policy support including ultra-long-term special bond quotas.
- Platform reduction continues: Zhenjiang, Jiangsu will reduce financing platforms by more than 90; Shandong will implement tiered management of city investment borrowing; Yunnan will reduce platform numbers; Jinhu County, Huai'an will continue platform transformation.

Minsheng Fixed Income chief Tan Yiming noted that 2024 debt management will follow "curb new increases, strictly pursue accountability, resolve existing stock" as the main framework across three levels.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"2023年地方化债，'下降'成关键词，凸显在五大方面：债务风险等级下降；债务规模、债务率下降，部分地区融资成本下降；积极争取特殊再融资债；争取隐债化解试点；部分地区平台数量大幅下降。"
</key_excerpts>

URL: https://www.21jingji.com/article/20260226/herald/cda1d96fcf143defd36dd326e36231e0.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a news article from 21st Century Business Herald (21世纪经济报道), published February 26, 2026, reporting on China's local government hidden debt resolution ("化债") results as revealed in the 2026 provincial government work reports across all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities.

**Key findings:**

1. **Hidden debt clearance expanding**: Xinjiang province announced full completion of existing hidden debt resolution at the provincial level. Multiple city/county-level areas achieved "hidden debt zeroing" including Gansu's Min County, Jilin's Siping, Heilongjiang's Heihe, Jiangsu's Lianyungang District, Fujian's Mingxi County, Liaoning's Tiedong District (which also completed dual-zeroing of financing platforms), Hunan's Wulingyuan and Sangzhi counties.

2. **Risk downgrades**: Following Inner Mongolia becoming the first province to exit key debt provinces in July 2025, Jilin announced its exit on January 27, 2026. Liaoning's Yingkou saw debt ratio drop 75 percentage points year-on-year; Benxi's Pingshan District exited the red high-risk list; Panjin removed its "full red zone" status; Inner Mongolia's Baotou and Wuhai moved from orange/red risk levels; Lanzhou achieved risk downgrades for 4 high-debt counties.

3. **Financing platform reductions**: Gansu removed 213 platforms (81.3% reduction), Liaoning reduced platforms by 85.2%, Hunan exited 304 platforms (annual task completion rate of 120%), Jiangxi exited 346 platforms (19 more than planned), Shaanxi pushed 170 platforms to exit. Per CSCI Pengyuan researcher Wu Zhiwu, Gansu and Liaoning each saw over 80% cumulative platform reduction.

4. **Debt swap results**: The Ministry of Finance reported that after debt swaps, average debt interest costs dropped by over 2.5 percentage points.

5. **Diversified resolution paths**: "Three-asset revitalization" (resources, assets, funds) proved significant—Jilin revitalized 110.87 billion yuan in idle assets in 2025; Hubei targeted 300+ billion yuan in revitalization; Hunan's Changde and Chenzhou saved substantial interest costs. "Clearing arrears to enterprises" also became a key focus, with 44+ cities disclosing progress. In 2025, 1,347.353 billion yuan in new special bonds were issued for clearing arrears (exceeding the 800 billion yuan hidden debt resolution quota), with over 700 billion yuan estimated for government arrears.

6. **Policy milestones**: The Ministry of Finance established a new Debt Management Department in November 2025, signaling centralized government debt management. Per the August 2024 central bank notice, end of June 2027 is a key deadline for platform exits. Jiangsu and Guizhou emphasized "preventing state-owned enterprises from spawning new platforms." CITIC Securities chief economist Ming Ming noted that since H2 2025, nominal-only platform exits have decreased while substantive asset-restructuring-based market transitions have increased significantly.

7. **2026 outlook**: Shaanxi aims for full hidden debt zeroing, Gansu plans to push eligible cities/counties to zero hidden debt early, and Jiangxi plans full exit of remaining financing platforms.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"融资平台退出明显加速，比如甘肃、辽宁退平台数量累计超过80%。再比如湖南退出304家，明显快于2024年，其中湖南桃源县通过盘活'三资'30.5亿元，压降平台数量8家，实现了融资平台数量的真实退出、而不是债务转移。" - 中证鹏元资深研究员吴志武, "各地置换后，债务平均利息成本降低超2.5个百分点，大大降低了地方政府负担。" - 财政部负责人, "2027年6月末不仅是平台退出的关键时点，也在某种程度上成为信用体系重构的新起点。" - 《关于规范退出融资平台公司的通知》(2024年8月央行等四部门), "2025年下半年以来，单纯名义上的'退平台'案例持续减少，依托实质性资产重组实现市场化转型的实践显著增加，'退平台'与真正的市场化转型正在加速并轨。" - 中信证券首席经济学家明明, "2025年首次通过新增专项债额度来置换地方政府拖欠款，且发行规模超出市场预期。2025年用于清欠的新增专项债规模达13473.53亿元，大幅超出当年用于隐性债务化解的8000亿元额度。" - 吴志武

--- SOURCE 3: 2025年三季度地方政府债券市场观察 ... ---
URL: https://www.lhratings.com/file/g0b9dd7e29c.pdf

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This document is a market observation report by 联合资信 (Lianhe Credit) on China's local government bond market for the first three quarters of 2025, authored by 唐立倩, 张永嘉, 董思茵, and 张英昊 of the Public Rating Department.

**KEY POLICY DEVELOPMENTS (2025):**
- The 2025 Government Work Report called for more proactive fiscal policy: deficit ratio raised to ~4% (up 1pp), deficit scale of 5.66 trillion yuan; planned issuance of 1.3 trillion yuan in ultra-long special treasury bonds, 500 billion yuan special treasury bonds (for major state banks' capital), and 4.4 trillion yuan new local government special bond quota (up 500 billion yuan). Total new government debt for 2025: 11.86 trillion yuan.
- Hidden debt swap: 6 trillion yuan special bond quota approved Nov 2024 to swap hidden debt, implemented over 3 years (2 trillion/year, 2024-2026); plus 800 billion yuan annually for 5 years from new special bonds. Total 10 trillion yuan in debt resolution resources.
- By end-Aug 2025, 4 trillion yuan of the 6 trillion quota had been issued. Local hidden debt fell from 14.3 trillion yuan (end-2023) to 10.5 trillion yuan (end-2024). Average debt interest cost down over 2.5 percentage points, saving over 450 billion yuan in interest.
- Financing platform counts and operating financial debt down 71% and 62% respectively vs March 2023 (as of Sept 2025).
- Inner Mongolia announced in July 2025 its exit from key debt provinces (first of 12 high-risk provinces); Ningxia and Jilin also pursuing exit.
- Land reserve special bonds resumed (Natural Resources Ministry + MOF notices, March 2025).
- "自审自发" (self-review and self-issuance) pilot program expanded.
- In October 2025, MOF advanced 500 billion yuan from existing local government debt quota to provinces, including support for major economic provinces' projects. 2026 advance quotas were issued earlier than usual.
- October 2025: 20th CPC Central Committee 4th Plenary Session and 15th Five-Year Plan recommendations emphasized strengthening fiscal sustainability and building a long-term government debt management mechanism.

**BOND MARKET DATA (Q1-Q3 2025):**
- Total issuance: 8.53 trillion yuan across 1,816 bonds, up 27.60% YoY — record high for the period. Net financing: 6.15 trillion yuan, up 54.24% YoY (from 3.99 trillion in 2024).
- Special bonds accounted for 75.96% of new issuance; new bonds 4.35 trillion yuan (+3.16%); refinancing bonds 4.18 trillion yuan (+69.28%), of which 1.99 trillion yuan was special refinancing for hidden debt swap (47.47% of refinancing; 99.50% of the 2 trillion annual quota completed).
- Land reserve special bonds: 2,804.76 billion yuan issued in first three quarters, accelerating in Q3 (1,096 billion yuan).
- Weighted average issuance tenor: 15.63 years (up from 14.43 in 2024); 10-year+ bonds = 75.71% of issuance (+6.83pp YoY). General bonds avg 8.80 years; special bonds avg 17.79 years.
- Top issuing regions: Jiangsu, Guangdong, Shandong (each >560 billion yuan). Guangdong, Zhejiang, Fujian led in new special bond shares (78.05%, 63.32%, 62.10%). "自审自发" pilot regions' new special bond share rose from 57.76% (2024) to 63.96%.
- 12 key debt provinces issued mostly refinancing bonds; their special refinancing/special bonds covered 30%+ of their end-2024 hidden debt by Oct 29, 2025.

**INTEREST RATES & SPREADS:**
- Average issuance yields by quarter 2025: Q1 1.94%, Q2 1.85%, Q3 2.01%. General bonds: 1.78%/1.72%/1.85%; special bonds: 1.98%/1.88%/2.05%.
- Average spreads widened sequentially through 2025: Q1 11.28bp, Q2 12.01bp, Q3 17.75bp.
- Q3 2025 highest 10-year spreads: Tianjin (35.00bp), Inner Mongolia (23.33bp), Hunan (23.25bp), Guizhou (21.67bp), Ningxia (21.00bp). Lowest: Beijing (5.00bp), Heilongjiang (8.20bp), Shanghai (10.00bp), Gansu (10.00bp). Guizhou saw largest MoM spread widening (+13.71bp); Beijing largest narrowing (-6.24bp).

**SPECIAL BOND USAGE (Q1-Q3 2025):**
- Top three uses: urban infrastructure (27.21%), transportation infrastructure (14.75%), urban-rural development (9.98%) — combined 51.95%. Land reserve special bonds accounted for 7.01% (2,158.29 billion yuan), issued in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangdong, Jiangsu, Sichuan, Hunan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Shandong, Anhui, Ningbo, Shenzhen, and Xiamen.

**Q4 2025 OUTLOOK:**
- Q4 supply pressure declines; provinces plan 1.26 trillion yuan in Q4 issuance (0.73 trillion new special bonds). Theoretical new debt space for Oct-Dec: 2.50 trillion yuan (excluding 2026's 2 trillion hidden debt swap quota), below last year's actual.
- Fiscal policy to maintain positive tone, funds tilted toward major economic provinces.
- Bond market rates expected to fluctuate downward within a range in Q4, influenced by PBOC resuming open-market treasury bond operations (Oct 27), US-China trade friction, stock market volatility, mutual fund fee reform, and anti-involution policies.
- Debt resolution philosophy: "坚持在发展中化债、在化债中发展" (resolve debt through development; develop through debt resolution). Total government debt at end-2024: 92.6 trillion yuan (central 34.6T, local statutory 47.5T, hidden 10.5T), government debt ratio 68.7% — below G20 average (118.2%) and G7 average (123.2%). MOF Minister Lan Fo'an: "化债是手段，发展是目的" (debt resolution is a means; development is the goal). During the 15th Five-Year Plan period, MOF will build a long-term government debt management mechanism compatible with high-quality development.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"截至2024年末，全国政府债务余额92.6万亿元（含法定债务和隐性债务）。其中，国债余额34.6万亿元，地方政府法定债务余额47.5万亿元，地方政府隐性债务余额10.5万亿元。" (As of end-2024, total national government debt was 92.6 trillion yuan, including 34.6T treasury bonds, 47.5T local statutory debt, and 10.5T local hidden debt.)

"内蒙古自治区于2025年7月宣布'要巩固退出地方债务重点省份成果'，意味着其已成为12个债务高风险省份中首个公开实现退出的地区。" (Inner Mongolia announced in July 2025 it would consolidate its exit from key debt province status, becoming the first of 12 high-risk debt provinces to publicly exit.)

"财政部部长蓝佛安指出，化债是手段，发展是目的，财政部坚持化债和发展两条腿走路，有效推动经济发展和债务管理良性循环。" (MOF Minister Lan Fo'an stated that debt resolution is a means while development is the goal, and the ministry persists in pursuing both debt resolution and development simultaneously.)

"总体看，我国政府负债率处于合理区间，风险安全可控。根据IMF今年4月发布的报告，G20国家平均政府负债率118.2%，G7国家平均政府负债率123.2%。" (Overall, China's government debt ratio of 68.7% is within a reasonable range and risks are safely controllable, compared to G20 average of 118.2% and G7 average of 123.2%.)

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is from the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) website (www.cppcc.gov.cn) and contains the full official text of the "Report on the Implementation of the 2024 Central and Local Budgets and the Draft 2025 Central and Local Budgets" (关于2024年中央和地方预算执行情况与2025年中央和地方预算草案的报告), delivered by the Ministry of Finance on March 5, 2025, at the Third Session of the 14th National People's Congress. SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage, published on the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Finance Department website on 2026-03-30, presents data on the 2025 fiscal revenue and expenditure situations across China's provinces, along with fiscal self-sufficiency rate rankings. Key findings include:

**Fiscal Revenue:** The six eastern provinces (Guangdong at 1.39 trillion yuan, Jiangsu at 1.02 trillion yuan, Zhejiang at 886.5 billion yuan, Shanghai at 850.1 billion yuan, Shandong at 786.4 billion yuan, and Beijing at 668.1 billion yuan) together generated approximately 5.6 trillion yuan in revenue, accounting for 46% of total local government revenue nationwide, making them the core pillar of national fiscal capacity.

SUMMARY:
<summary>
**中央转移支付 (Central Transfer Payments) - Baidu Baike Encyclopedia Entry**

This webpage is a Baidu Baike encyclopedia entry defining and detailing China's "central transfer payment" (中央转移支付) system — a national fiscal policy implemented to coordinate balanced regional socioeconomic development and ensure equalization of basic public services.

**Definition & Origins:**
- Central transfer payments are China's primary regional compensation policy, used widely worldwide to narrow regional development gaps.
- The system operates by higher-level governments making free (non-repayable) fund allocations to lower-level governments to address regional fiscal imbalances.
- Originated from the 1994 tax-sharing system reform (分税制改革).
- Includes three categories: general transfer payments (均衡财力), special transfer payments (定向支持特定领域), and co-financing transfer payments (共同财政事权, established in 2019).

**Historical Development:**
- 1994: Tax-sharing system reform began; transfer payment system trial implementation to ensure equal access to education, health, and environmental services.
- 2014: State Council pushed reform establishing general transfer payments as the dominant structure.
- 2020: Fiscal fund direct-arrival mechanism created.
- 2023: Central-to-local transfer payments reached 10.06 trillion yuan.

**Key Statistics & Recent Data:**
- 2025: Budget allocated 10.34 trillion yuan (same-caliber growth of 8.4%), focusing on increasing general transfer payments to strengthen local fiscal capacity (announced by Finance Minister Lan Fo'an on March 6, 2025).
- 2025 actual execution: 101,925.14 billion yuan (10.19 trillion), exceeding central-level general public revenue for the first time; third consecutive year above 10 trillion.
- 2026: Budget increased to 10.4 trillion yuan (10.42 trillion), a record high — fourth consecutive year above 10 trillion.
- Six transfer payment methods: tax rebates, original system subsidies, special subsidies, various settlement subsidies, and other subsidies.

**Distribution by Province (2025 execution data):**
- 10 provinces received over 400 billion yuan each, led by: Sichuan (684 billion), Henan (~596.8 billion), Xinjiang (incl. Corps, ~529 billion), Hunan, Hubei, Hebei, Heilongjiang, Yunnan, Anhui, Guangxi.
- Funds primarily flowed to central, western, and northeastern regions; eastern six provinces (Guangdong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Shanghai, Shandong, Beijing) received only ~1.2 trillion total (~12% of total).
- Per-capita transfer payments highest in: Tibet (over 70,000 yuan), Xinjiang, Qinghai, Ningxia, Heilongjiang. Sichuan: 8,200 yuan; Henan: 6,100 yuan; Guangdong (largest economy): only 2,070 yuan — lowest nationally.
- Net contributors: Guangdong, Shanghai, Beijing, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Shandong, Fujian, Tianjin — with Guangdong contributing ~800 billion yuan net in 2025.

**Latest Policy Developments (2025-2026):**
- Since 2024, a "high-quality development incentive fund" of 50 billion yuan annually was added to transfer payments (纳入县级基本财力保障机制奖补资金).
- In 2025, a new "central fiscal childcare subsidy" was established — 300 yuan/month per infant under 3 years old, with central government covering 90%; Guangdong received 9.058 billion yuan (~10% of total) due to its high infant population.
- For 2026: plans to continue the 500 billion incentive fund, reduce some special transfer payments to increase local fiscal capacity transfers, and pilot consolidated utilization of transfer funds in selected provinces.

**Challenges/Issues (historical context):**
- Problems identified post-1994 reform: unclear division of governmental powers, irrational transfer support structure, imbalanced sub-provincial fiscal systems, and low legal authority level of transfer payment regulations.
- The reform goal includes not just easing grassroots fiscal strain but building a self-regulating grassroots fiscal system.

**Sources cited** include Finance Ministry reports, China People's Congress website, Jiemian News (界面新闻), CBN (第一财经), Fenghuang, and ZAKER, dated between 2015 and 2026.
</summary>
