--- SOURCE 3: 2025年三季度地方政府债券市场观察 ... ---
URL: https://www.lhratings.com/file/g0b9dd7e29c.pdf

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This document is a market observation report by 联合资信 (Lianhe Credit) on China's local government bond market for the first three quarters of 2025, authored by 唐立倩, 张永嘉, 董思茵, and 张英昊 of the Public Rating Department.

**KEY POLICY DEVELOPMENTS (2025):**
- The 2025 Government Work Report called for more proactive fiscal policy: deficit ratio raised to ~4% (up 1pp), deficit scale of 5.66 trillion yuan; planned issuance of 1.3 trillion yuan in ultra-long special treasury bonds, 500 billion yuan special treasury bonds (for major state banks' capital), and 4.4 trillion yuan new local government special bond quota (up 500 billion yuan). Total new government debt for 2025: 11.86 trillion yuan.
- Hidden debt swap: 6 trillion yuan special bond quota approved Nov 2024 to swap hidden debt, implemented over 3 years (2 trillion/year, 2024-2026); plus 800 billion yuan annually for 5 years from new special bonds. Total 10 trillion yuan in debt resolution resources.
- By end-Aug 2025, 4 trillion yuan of the 6 trillion quota had been issued. Local hidden debt fell from 14.3 trillion yuan (end-2023) to 10.5 trillion yuan (end-2024). Average debt interest cost down over 2.5 percentage points, saving over 450 billion yuan in interest.
- Financing platform counts and operating financial debt down 71% and 62% respectively vs March 2023 (as of Sept 2025).
- Inner Mongolia announced in July 2025 its exit from key debt provinces (first of 12 high-risk provinces); Ningxia and Jilin also pursuing exit.
- Land reserve special bonds resumed (Natural Resources Ministry + MOF notices, March 2025).
- "自审自发" (self-review and self-issuance) pilot program expanded.
- In October 2025, MOF advanced 500 billion yuan from existing local government debt quota to provinces, including support for major economic provinces' projects. 2026 advance quotas were issued earlier than usual.
- October 2025: 20th CPC Central Committee 4th Plenary Session and 15th Five-Year Plan recommendations emphasized strengthening fiscal sustainability and building a long-term government debt management mechanism.

**BOND MARKET DATA (Q1-Q3 2025):**
- Total issuance: 8.53 trillion yuan across 1,816 bonds, up 27.60% YoY — record high for the period. Net financing: 6.15 trillion yuan, up 54.24% YoY (from 3.99 trillion in 2024).
- Special bonds accounted for 75.96% of new issuance; new bonds 4.35 trillion yuan (+3.16%); refinancing bonds 4.18 trillion yuan (+69.28%), of which 1.99 trillion yuan was special refinancing for hidden debt swap (47.47% of refinancing; 99.50% of the 2 trillion annual quota completed).
- Land reserve special bonds: 2,804.76 billion yuan issued in first three quarters, accelerating in Q3 (1,096 billion yuan).
- Weighted average issuance tenor: 15.63 years (up from 14.43 in 2024); 10-year+ bonds = 75.71% of issuance (+6.83pp YoY). General bonds avg 8.80 years; special bonds avg 17.79 years.
- Top issuing regions: Jiangsu, Guangdong, Shandong (each >560 billion yuan). Guangdong, Zhejiang, Fujian led in new special bond shares (78.05%, 63.32%, 62.10%). "自审自发" pilot regions' new special bond share rose from 57.76% (2024) to 63.96%.
- 12 key debt provinces issued mostly refinancing bonds; their special refinancing/special bonds covered 30%+ of their end-2024 hidden debt by Oct 29, 2025.

**INTEREST RATES & SPREADS:**
- Average issuance yields by quarter 2025: Q1 1.94%, Q2 1.85%, Q3 2.01%. General bonds: 1.78%/1.72%/1.85%; special bonds: 1.98%/1.88%/2.05%.
- Average spreads widened sequentially through 2025: Q1 11.28bp, Q2 12.01bp, Q3 17.75bp.
- Q3 2025 highest 10-year spreads: Tianjin (35.00bp), Inner Mongolia (23.33bp), Hunan (23.25bp), Guizhou (21.67bp), Ningxia (21.00bp). Lowest: Beijing (5.00bp), Heilongjiang (8.20bp), Shanghai (10.00bp), Gansu (10.00bp). Guizhou saw largest MoM spread widening (+13.71bp); Beijing largest narrowing (-6.24bp).

**SPECIAL BOND USAGE (Q1-Q3 2025):**
- Top three uses: urban infrastructure (27.21%), transportation infrastructure (14.75%), urban-rural development (9.98%) — combined 51.95%. Land reserve special bonds accounted for 7.01% (2,158.29 billion yuan), issued in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangdong, Jiangsu, Sichuan, Hunan, Fujian, Zhejiang, Shandong, Anhui, Ningbo, Shenzhen, and Xiamen.

**Q4 2025 OUTLOOK:**
- Q4 supply pressure declines; provinces plan 1.26 trillion yuan in Q4 issuance (0.73 trillion new special bonds). Theoretical new debt space for Oct-Dec: 2.50 trillion yuan (excluding 2026's 2 trillion hidden debt swap quota), below last year's actual.
- Fiscal policy to maintain positive tone, funds tilted toward major economic provinces.
- Bond market rates expected to fluctuate downward within a range in Q4, influenced by PBOC resuming open-market treasury bond operations (Oct 27), US-China trade friction, stock market volatility, mutual fund fee reform, and anti-involution policies.
- Debt resolution philosophy: "坚持在发展中化债、在化债中发展" (resolve debt through development; develop through debt resolution). Total government debt at end-2024: 92.6 trillion yuan (central 34.6T, local statutory 47.5T, hidden 10.5T), government debt ratio 68.7% — below G20 average (118.2%) and G7 average (123.2%). MOF Minister Lan Fo'an: "化债是手段，发展是目的" (debt resolution is a means; development is the goal). During the 15th Five-Year Plan period, MOF will build a long-term government debt management mechanism compatible with high-quality development.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"截至2024年末，全国政府债务余额92.6万亿元（含法定债务和隐性债务）。其中，国债余额34.6万亿元，地方政府法定债务余额47.5万亿元，地方政府隐性债务余额10.5万亿元。" (As of end-2024, total national government debt was 92.6 trillion yuan, including 34.6T treasury bonds, 47.5T local statutory debt, and 10.5T local hidden debt.)

"2025年前三季度，地方政府债券累计发行8.53万亿元，较上年同期增长27.60%，发行规模及净融资额创历史同期新高；其中用于置换隐性债务的政府专项债券发行1.99万亿元，2万亿隐债置换已近尾声。" (Local government bonds totaled 8.53 trillion yuan in Q1-Q3 2025, up 27.60% YoY, a record high; 1.99 trillion yuan was issued for hidden debt swap, nearing completion of the 2 trillion target.)

"内蒙古自治区于2025年7月宣布'要巩固退出地方债务重点省份成果'，意味着其已成为12个债务高风险省份中首个公开实现退出的地区。" (Inner Mongolia announced in July 2025 it would consolidate its exit from key debt province status, becoming the first of 12 high-risk debt provinces to publicly exit.)

"财政部部长蓝佛安指出，化债是手段，发展是目的，财政部坚持化债和发展两条腿走路，有效推动经济发展和债务管理良性循环。" (MOF Minister Lan Fo'an stated that debt resolution is a means while development is the goal, and the ministry persists in pursuing both debt resolution and development simultaneously.)

"总体看，我国政府负债率处于合理区间，风险安全可控。根据IMF今年4月发布的报告，G20国家平均政府负债率118.2%，G7国家平均政府负债率123.2%。" (Overall, China's government debt ratio of 68.7% is within a reasonable range and risks are safely controllable, compared to G20 average of 118.2% and G7 average of 123.2%.)
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 4: 地方化债最新进展：超82%融资平台退出、经营性金融债务下降超74% ---
URL: https://topics.caixin.com/m/2026-03-05/102419842.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Caixin (财新) news article published on March 5, 2026, reporting on the latest progress of China's local government debt resolution ("化债") efforts. The article, written by journalist 于海荣, details findings from the "2025 National Economic and Social Development Plan Implementation and 2026 Plan Draft Report" (计划报告) submitted to the 14th National People's Congress 4th Session on March 5, 2026.

Key data points from the report's review of 2025 achievements:
- 2 trillion yuan in refinancing bonds were issued to replace existing hidden local government debt, reducing average interest costs by more than 2.5 percentage points
- 800 billion yuan in new local government special bonds were arranged to supplement local government fund budgets and support debt resolution
- Over 82% of local financing vehicles (融资平台) have exited the market
- The scale of existing operating financial debt held by financing vehicles declined by more than 74%

The article notes that for 2026, China plans multiple measures to address operating debt risks of local government financing platforms, and will stage-by-stage, category-by-category increase support ratios for certain areas of "two major constructions" (两重建设) and central budget investments to reduce local funding pressure.

The article includes related reading links, notably a Caixin Weekly feature from February 21, 2026 titled "2026 Local Debt Resolution Map" (2026年地方化债图谱), and an English-language version of the article on Caixin Global.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"重点领域风险化解取得积极进展。地方政府债务风险化解扎实推进，发行用于置换存量隐性债务的再融资债券2万亿元，置换后平均利息成本降低2.5个百分点以上，安排8000亿元新增地方政府专项债券补充地方政府性基金财力、支持化债，超82%的融资平台实现退出，融资平台存量经营性金融债务规模下降超74%。"

--- SOURCE 5: 关于2024年中央和地方预算执行情况与2025年 ... ---
URL: http://www.cppcc.gov.cn/zxww/2025/03/14/ARTI1741913781118109.shtml

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is from the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference (CPPCC) website (www.cppcc.gov.cn) and contains the full official text of the "Report on the Implementation of the 2024 Central and Local Budgets and the Draft 2025 Central and Local Budgets" (关于2024年中央和地方预算执行情况与2025年中央和地方预算草案的报告), delivered by the Ministry of Finance on March 5, 2025, at the Third Session of the 14th National People's Congress. The report was published on the CPPCC website on March 14, 2025, sourced from Xinhua News Agency.

**2024 Budget Execution Highlights:**
- National general public budget revenue: 21.97 trillion yuan (98.1% of budget, up 1.3% from 2023); tax revenue 17.5 trillion yuan (down 3.4%); non-tax revenue 4.47 trillion yuan (up 25.4%)

SUMMARY:
<summary>
**中央转移支付 (Central Transfer Payments) - Baidu Baike Encyclopedia Entry**

This webpage is a Baidu Baike encyclopedia entry defining and detailing China's "central transfer payment" (中央转移支付) system — a national fiscal policy implemented to coordinate balanced regional socioeconomic development and ensure equalization of basic public services.

**Definition & Origins:**
- Central transfer payments are China's primary regional compensation policy, used widely worldwide to narrow regional development gaps.
- The system operates by higher-level governments making free (non-repayable) fund allocations to lower-level governments to address regional fiscal imbalances.
- Originated from the 1994 tax-sharing system reform (分税制改革).
- Includes three categories: general transfer payments (均衡财力), special transfer payments (定向支持特定领域), and co-financing transfer payments (共同财政事权, established in 2019).

**Historical Development:**
- 1994: Tax-sharing system reform began; transfer payment system trial implementation to ensure equal access to education, health, and environmental services.
- 2014: State Council pushed reform establishing general transfer payments as the dominant structure.
- 2020: Fiscal fund direct-arrival mechanism created.
- 2023: Central-to-local transfer payments reached 10.06 trillion yuan.

**Key Statistics & Recent Data:**
- 2025: Budget allocated 10.34 trillion yuan (same-caliber growth of 8.4%), focusing on increasing general transfer payments to strengthen local fiscal capacity (announced by Finance Minister Lan Fo'an on March 6, 2025).
- 2025 actual execution: 101,925.14 billion yuan (10.19 trillion), exceeding central-level general public revenue for the first time; third consecutive year above 10 trillion.
- 2026: Budget increased to 10.4 trillion yuan (10.42 trillion), a record high — fourth consecutive year above 10 trillion.
- Six transfer payment methods: tax rebates, original system subsidies, special subsidies, various settlement subsidies, and other subsidies.

**Distribution by Province (2025 execution data):**
- 10 provinces received over 400 billion yuan each, led by: Sichuan (684 billion), Henan (~596.8 billion), Xinjiang (incl. Corps, ~529 billion), Hunan, Hubei, Hebei, Heilongjiang, Yunnan, Anhui, Guangxi.
- Funds primarily flowed to central, western, and northeastern regions; eastern six provinces (Guangdong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Shanghai, Shandong, Beijing) received only ~1.2 trillion total (~12% of total).
- Per-capita transfer payments highest in: Tibet (over 70,000 yuan), Xinjiang, Qinghai, Ningxia, Heilongjiang. Sichuan: 8,200 yuan; Henan: 6,100 yuan; Guangdong (largest economy): only 2,070 yuan — lowest nationally.
- Net contributors: Guangdong, Shanghai, Beijing, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Shandong, Fujian, Tianjin — with Guangdong contributing ~800 billion yuan net in 2025.

**Latest Policy Developments (2025-2026):**
- Since 2024, a "high-quality development incentive fund" of 50 billion yuan annually was added to transfer payments (纳入县级基本财力保障机制奖补资金).
- In 2025, a new "central fiscal childcare subsidy" was established — 300 yuan/month per infant under 3 years old, with central government covering 90%; Guangdong received 9.058 billion yuan (~10% of total) due to its high infant population.
- For 2026: plans to continue the 500 billion incentive fund, reduce some special transfer payments to increase local fiscal capacity transfers, and pilot consolidated utilization of transfer funds in selected provinces.

**Challenges/Issues (historical context):**
- Problems identified post-1994 reform: unclear division of governmental powers, irrational transfer support structure, imbalanced sub-provincial fiscal systems, and low legal authority level of transfer payment regulations.
- The reform goal includes not just easing grassroots fiscal strain but building a self-regulating grassroots fiscal system.

**Sources cited** include Finance Ministry reports, China People's Congress website, Jiemian News (界面新闻), CBN (第一财经), Fenghuang, and ZAKER, dated between 2015 and 2026.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 1: 关于增发万亿国债，财政部最新解读来了！ ---
URL: https://wallstreetcn.com/articles/3700428

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a news article from 华尔街见闻 (Wallstreetcn.com) published on October 25, 2023, by reporter 卜淑情, covering China's Ministry of Finance (财政部) briefing on the issuance of an additional 1 trillion yuan (1万亿) in treasury bonds (国债).

**Key Details:**

**Overview:** The central government will issue an additional 1 trillion yuan in 2023 treasury bonds in the fourth quarter of this year. All proceeds will be allocated to local governments via transfer payments to support post-disaster recovery and reconstruction, and to strengthen disaster prevention, mitigation, and relief capabilities.

**Fiscal Impact:**
- National fiscal deficit will rise from 3.88 trillion yuan to 4.88 trillion yuan
- Central government deficit will rise from 3.16 trillion yuan to 4.16 trillion yuan
- Fiscal deficit ratio will increase from approximately 3% to approximately 3.8%
- The government debt ratio remains within a reasonable range, with overall risk controllable

**Key Decisions (from Vice Minister of Finance 朱忠明):**
- The bonds will be issued through public offering and coordinated with the already-scheduled annual treasury bond issuance
- The central government will bear principal and interest repayment - no burden added to local governments
- The 1 trillion yuan will be used over two years: 500 billion yuan in 2023 and 500 billion yuan carried over to 2024
- A dedicated transfer payment project titled "Post-disaster Recovery and Reconstruction and Enhancement of Disaster Prevention, Mitigation and Relief Capacity Subsidy Funds" will be established
- Bond issuance will be coordinated with fund usage progress to avoid idle funds
- All treasury bond funds will be placed under direct-funding (直达资金) mechanism for full-process monitoring

**Eight Funding Directions (8个方向):**
1. Post-disaster recovery and reconstruction, prioritizing the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei (京津冀) region in North China
2. Key flood control projects in northern regions, focusing on the Haihe and Songhua River basins (including major river embankments, large/medium reservoirs, flood detention areas)
3. Natural disaster emergency response capability enhancement projects
4. Other key flood control projects (tributaries, small/medium rivers, mountain torrent control, reservoir reinforcement)
5. Irrigation district construction/renovation and key soil erosion control projects
6. Urban drainage and flood prevention capability improvement
7. Key comprehensive natural disaster prevention systems
8. High-standard farmland construction in Northeast China and Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei disaster-affected areas

**Project Requirements (from NDRC's 罗国三):**
- Projects must comply with plans or implementation schemes (priority to "14th Five-Year Plan" projects)
- Must meet investment direction requirements - no general competitive industrial projects, government buildings, image projects, or vanity projects
- Projects must have mature preparatory work; new projects should start construction as soon as possible, with urgent projects completed before next year's flood season
- Complex major projects should not start later than end of June next year
- Funds must match construction progress

**Background Context:**
- The decision follows the August 17 Central Politburo Standing Committee meeting on flood prevention, disaster relief, and post-disaster recovery
- The proposal was approved by the 14th National People's Congress Standing Committee's 6th session
- Triggered by severe rainfall, flooding, and typhoon disasters across multiple regions in 2023, including the "23·7" extreme flood event in the Haihe River basin (July 29-August 2)
- 国家发改委 is drafting the "Plan for Post-disaster Recovery and Reconstruction and Enhancing Disaster Prevention Capability in North China, with focus on Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei"
- NDRC and MOF will establish a working mechanism with 15+ ministries for project screening, implementation, and supervision
- Supervision measures include online monitoring, on-site inspections, and serious accountability for fund misappropriation

**Notable Answers:**
- When asked if breaking the 3% deficit red line signals that central government prefers to leverage rather than local governments, MOF stated the deficit increase is modest and risk remains controllable
- The 1 trillion bond issuance is NOT primarily an economic stimulus measure but rather to support disaster recovery per Central Politburo decisions, though it will objectively boost domestic demand
- Central fiscal subsidies/standards for relevant sectors will be appropriately raised to reduce local funding pressure
</summary>

"考虑到本次增发的国债是纳入到中央财政赤字管理，将采取公开发行方式发行，和已经确定的年度国债发行进行统筹安排。增发国债由中央承担还本付息，并将于今明两年安排使用，2023年安排使用5000亿元，结转2024年使用5000亿元。"
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 1: 财税研究所 ---
URL: http://ipft.ruc.edu.cn/yjcg/sdpl/5c30ea5c2e4d43e8bf0673853fa7b34a.htm

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article, published in the "International Taxation" (《国际税收》) journal's 2025 issue No. 8, is authored by Yue Shumin (岳树民), a professor at Renmin University of China's School of Finance and a senior researcher at the Finance and Taxation Research Institute, and Wang Li (王荔), a doctoral student at Renmin University of China. The article examines the goals, implementation paths, challenges, and countermeasures for China's consumption tax (excise duty) system reform.

KEY CONTENT:

**Historical Background:** China's consumption tax (特别消费税/Excise Duty) was established in 1994 as a special consumption tax levied on selected consumer goods on top of VAT, primarily to regulate consumption structure, control pollution, protect the environment, and secure fiscal revenue. Major reforms occurred in 2003 (expanding the tax base), 2013 (adjusting tax scope, categories, and rates, including high energy-consuming and high-pollution products), 2016 (imposing consumption tax on ultra-luxury cars at retail stage), 2019 (State Council plan to move consumption tax collection to later stages and devolve it to local governments), and 2024 (the 20th CPC Central Committee's Third Plenary Session explicitly proposed "advancing the backward movement of consumption tax collection stages and steadily devolving it to local governments").

**Key Statistics:** In 2023, domestic consumption tax revenue was approximately 1.6 trillion yuan (8.9% of total tax revenue), while domestic VAT was about 6.9 trillion yuan (38% of total tax revenue), a ratio of roughly 1:4 (compared to OECD's ~1:3 ratio). In 2023, central government fiscal expenditure accounted for 13.9% and local government 86.1%, while central revenue was 45.9% and local 54.1%. Local fiscal revenue was about 11.7 trillion yuan, with local autonomous revenue of about 5.06 trillion yuan (43.2%).

**Reform Goals:** (1) Enhance regulatory functions; (2) Enhance revenue functions; (3) Establish a foundation for improving central-local fiscal relations by increasing local autonomous fiscal capacity.

**Implementation Paths:** (1) Appropriately expand the tax base (including high-sugar/high-fat/high-salt foods, high energy-consuming/polluting goods, high-substitution resource-energy goods, and some luxury goods); (2) Optimize tax rate structure (higher rates for non-green goods with substitutes and suppressed goods; moderate rates for luxury goods; lower rates for widely consumed goods; minimize rate tiers for administrability); (3) Move collection from production/import stage to wholesale/retail stage, advancing step-by-step ("条件合适" for collection stage movement, "过程稳妥" for revenue devolution).

**Challenges:** (1) Tax compliance issues from moving collection to wholesale/retail (especially for small businesses and individual proprietors); (2) Tax administration difficulties (more dispersed taxpayers, higher management costs); (3) Multi-sales-model and multi-business-format management issues (e.g., online direct sales, platform sales, distinguishing wholesale from retail, consumption location determination); (4) New interest incentive mechanisms from revenue devolution (potential regional fiscal imbalances, risk of local governments encouraging consumption of restricted goods).

**Proposed Countermeasures:** (1) Adopt a "small steps" approach—advance reforms selectively for goods with clear identification and controllability (e.g., tobacco, alcohol, gold/silver jewelry, high-end cosmetics, high-end watches); (2) Use a systematic perspective to coordinate VAT and consumption tax reforms, establish transitional transfer payment mechanisms, and carefully time the devolution of revenues from strongly-suppressed goods like cigarettes (which already have established social constraints against consumption); (3) Improve compliance and administration through digital tax management systems (including government-provided digital systems for small businesses and smart tax systems using product identity codes and information-sharing platforms, drawing on the refined oil industry's management model); (4) Give appropriate consideration to small businesses and individual proprietors—recommending consumption tax exemption aligned with VAT threshold policies for ordinary daily-goods shops, but not for specialized sellers of tobacco, alcohol, luxury watches, gold/jewelry, etc.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"推进消费税征收环节后移并稳步下划地方"是我国新一轮财税体制改革的重要任务，兼具健全现代税收制度、增强地方自主财力、完善中央地方财政关系等多重目的。—党的二十届三中全会改革要求
</key_excerpts>

URL: https://economy.caixin.com/2024-07-31/102221775.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Caixin.com (财新网) news article published on July 31, 2024, reporting on China's Ministry of Finance (MOF) announcement regarding the reform of the consumption tax and local tax system.

**Key Points:**

1. **Main Announcement**: The MOF stated it will consider moving the collection point of the consumption tax (消费税) backward to the retail stage and steadily devolving it to local governments, to be implemented in a staged, item-by-item (分品目、分步骤) manner.

2. **Additional Tax Reforms Announced**:
   - Merging the urban maintenance and construction tax (城市维护建设税), education surcharge (教育费附加), and local education surcharge (地方教育附加) into a single "local surtax" (地方附加税)
   - Adding volatile organic compounds (VOCs/挥发性有机物) to the scope of the environmental protection tax (环保税)

3. **Background Context**: 
   - The announcement follows the Third Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee (二十届三中全会), which outlined reforms to expand local tax sources and increase local fiscal autonomy
   - The plenum's "Decision" document explicitly called for increasing local self-raised fiscal capacity, expanding local tax sources, and appropriately expanding local tax administration authority
   - MOF Vice Minister Wang Dongwei (王东伟) made the remarks at a State Council Information Office press conference on "promoting high-quality development"
   - Wang noted that as China transitions to high-quality development, problems with the current local tax system are becoming increasingly prominent, including an imperfect system, unreasonable structure, and inadequate tax power allocation

4. **Related Issues**: The article also mentions standardizing non-tax revenue management and appropriately delegating some non-tax revenue management authority to localities for differentiated management based on local conditions.

**Author/Publication Details**: Written by Caixin reporter 程思炜 (Cheng Siwei), edited by 于海荣 (Yu Hairong), published on July 31, 2024, under the Economy > News section of Caixin.com.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 3: 两会专栏 | 田志伟：2025政府工作报告解读——推进消费税征税环节后移、增加地方政府自主财力 ---
URL: https://cmi.sufe.edu.cn/9c/aa/c12152a236714/page.htm

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a policy analysis article from the Institute for Chinese-style Modernization (中国式现代化研究院) at Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, published on March 6, 2025. The author is Tian Zhiwei (田志伟), a special research fellow at the institute, interpreting two key fiscal reform measures from China's 2025 Government Work Report.

The article analyzes two main topics:

**1. Moving consumption tax collection forward (消费税征收环节后移并下划地方)**

- The 2025 Government Work Report calls for accelerating the shift of consumption tax collection for certain categories from production to wholesale/retail stages, and allocating it to local governments to increase local fiscal autonomy.
- This builds on a 2019 State Council notice and the 2024 Third Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, which both proposed similar reforms.
- The 2019 plan targeted high-end watches, precious jewelry, and jade/gemstones first, but these categories generate limited revenue and cannot solve current local fiscal pressures.
- Consumption tax has 15 categories (烟/含 tobacco, refined oil, automobiles, alcohol), but most revenue comes from four: tobacco, alcohol, refined oil, and automobiles.
- Current collection is at production stage mainly for administrative convenience, but this has caused tax evasion issues (e.g., companies artificially lowering factory prices to related entities).
- From an administrative control perspective, the feasibility ranking for moving collection downstream is: tobacco (best, due to monopoly sales management), automobiles, refined oil, and alcohol (hardest).
- However, since automobiles play a key role in stimulating consumption, moving automobile tax downstream is less likely. The author suggests lowering the threshold for luxury car retail-stage taxation from 1.3 million yuan to 800,000 yuan.

**2. Establishing incentive mechanisms to cultivate local fiscal resources**

- Debates on future local tax systems include property tax, consumption tax, environmental protection tax, and personal income tax as candidates for main local taxes, but none has achieved consensus.
- The author argues that, in the long term, a property tax-based local tax system is most appropriate because it aligns the interests of local governments and residents — governments improve public services to collect more property tax, while residents "vote with their feet" to choose where to live.
- However, this requires institutional support such as lowering transaction costs for residents to move (reducing real estate transaction taxes), to prevent governments from exploiting residents' high relocation costs by lowering public service quality.
- The Government Work Report's call to "actively explore establishing incentive mechanisms" allows local governments to independently explore within limited scope, using decentralization to encourage local governments to actively seek tax sources and relieve fiscal pressure.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
2025年的《政府工作报告》指出要“加快推进部分品目消费税征收环节后移并下划地方，增加地方自主财力”，要“积极探索建立激励机制，促进地方在高质量发展中培育财源”。
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 4: 消费税征收环节后移并稳步下划地方的推进情况及审计对策 ... ---
URL: https://www.audit.gov.cn/n6/n39/c10784298/content.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is from the official website of the National Audit Office of the People's Republic of China (审计署), specifically from the "Audit Research" (审计科研) section of the "Audit Window" (审计之窗) channel. The page contains a research article titled "消费税征收环节后移并稳步下划地方的推进情况及审计对策建议" (Progress on Shifting the Consumption Tax Collection Stage Backward and Steadily Allocating It to Local Governments, and Audit Countermeasure Suggestions), authored by 戎梅 (Rong Mei) and published on May 9, 2026, by the Audit Research Institute of the National Audit Office.

Key content of the article:
- The consumption tax has been levied since 1994 and has undergone 6 adjustments to its collection stage. Currently, it is primarily collected at the production stage, with all revenue belonging to the central government.
- In 2019, the reform task of shifting the consumption tax collection stage backward and allocating it to local governments was first proposed.
- The 14th Five-Year Plan (2021) and the Third Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee (2024) made important deployments for this reform.
- The 2025 Government Work Report proposed "accelerating" the consumption tax reform.
- The reform requires completing 4 specific tasks:
  1. Selecting tax items for shifting the collection stage backward based on the principle of controllable collection and management;
  2. Rationally determining the "base year," "base number," and "increment" calculation calibers;

This article from Qiushi Network (求是网), published October 13, 2024, outlines the main tasks for deepening China's fiscal and tax system reform as mandated by the Third Plenary Session of the 20th Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (item 17 of the Decision). The reform is divided into three main areas:

1. **Improving the budget system**: Strengthen fiscal science management with greater systematization, refinement, standardization, and rule-of-law orientation. This includes bringing all revenue derived from administrative power, government credit, and state-owned resources into government budget management; deepening zero-based budget reform; unifying budget allocation authority; improving expenditure standards; implementing accrual-based government comprehensive financial reporting; and following the principle of "small money frugal, big money generous" to prioritize funding for national strategic tasks and basic livelihood needs.

2. **Improving the tax system**: Strengthen the regulatory function of taxation to promote high-quality development, social fairness, and market unity. This includes optimizing the tax structure to adapt to digitalization and green development trends; comprehensively implementing water resource fee-to-tax conversion; improving the direct tax system and individual income tax (unified taxation of labor income); implementing the principle of statutory taxation with steady progress on VAT, consumption tax, and non-tax revenue legislation; and standardizing tax incentive policies to create a unified, fair domestic market environment.

3. **Improving central-local fiscal relations**: Increase local autonomous fiscal capacity by expanding local tax sources, moving consumption tax collection backward and allocating it to local governments; merging urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, and local education surcharge into a local surtax; improving the fiscal transfer payment system by standardizing special transfers and increasing general transfers; managing local government debt by expanding special bond support scope and establishing a full-caliber local debt monitoring system; strengthening central fiscal authority and increasing the central government's expenditure ratio; and prohibiting illegal requirements for local matching funds.

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This BBC Chinese article (published September 15, 2023) examines why China's property tax (房地产税) has been shelved despite local government fiscal crises stemming from declining land-sale revenues. Key points:

**Context:** China's economic recovery after pandemic restrictions was weak, especially in real estate. On September 6, 2023, the 14th National People's Congress Standing Committee released its five-year legislative plan, which did NOT include the property tax law in any of its three categories (79 draft laws ready for review, 51 needing further work, and items requiring continued research). This surprised observers because a draft had already circulated for comments in 2021, and in October 2021 the NPC authorized the State Council to pilot property tax reforms in selected regions.

**Why the property tax was proposed:** China's 20-year real estate boom saw both developers over-borrowing and local governments earning huge revenues from land sales. When asset returns couldn't cover interest, Ponzi-style "borrowing new to repay old" financing emerged. In 2020, policies cooling the property market led to crises at Evergrande, Country Garden, and others, with local government land-transfer revenues sharply declining. The property tax was seen as an ideal replacement revenue source for land-dependent local finances. Additionally, after the business tax-to-VAT reform under Xi Jinping, local governments had fewer tax sources and needed a self-controlled tax. Xi also framed the property tax as serving "common prosperity" (共同富裕) to prevent polarization, writing about this in the party journal Qiushi.

**Timeline of attempts:**
- 2011: First pilot property taxes launched in Shanghai (targeting multi-home residents) and Chongqing (targeting high-end luxury homes)
- 2017: Then-Finance Minister Xiao Jie set a timeline for completing legislative procedures by 2019 and implementation by 2020 — this failed
- October 23, 2021: NPC Standing Committee authorized the State Council to conduct property tax reform pilots in certain regions, covering residential and non-residential properties, with a five-year pilot period — but no further action followed
- 2023: Latest legislative plan omits the property tax entirely, suggesting no implementation for at least five more years

**Current context:** In June-July 2023, sales by China's 100 largest developers fell about 30% year-on-year. In late July, the Politburo meeting unusually omitted the "housing is for living, not speculation" (房住不炒) phrase, signaling easing. On August 25, 2023, regulators issued the "recognition of housing not loans" (认房不认贷) policy easing first-home mortgage rules. Launching a property tax now could disrupt this fragile recovery.

**Controversies and expert views:**
- Double taxation: Residents already pay for 70-year land use rights; taxing them again constitutes double taxation since transaction-phase taxes (land value-added tax, urban construction tax, farmland occupation tax) are already passed on to buyers
- Legal issue: China's land is state-owned, not private, unlike Western property tax systems where property is privately owned — so taxing land arguably should be paid by the state (landowner), not residents
- Former State Taxation Administration deputy director Xu Shanda noted two difficulties: (1) land values appreciate while buildings depreciate, making a unified tax base hard; (2) land is state-owned while buildings are privately owned, making a unified tax on two different subjects challenging
- CUHK Associate Professor Yang Yang said in oversupplied cities property prices could fall, but in first-tier cities where demand exceeds supply, prices unlikely to drop — the tax would just be passed on to buyers or rents
</summary>

SUMMARY:

This article (published July 18, 2016, from 上观新闻/Shanghai Observer, by 王红茹) examines why China's property tax (房地产税) has not been implemented after 13 years of deliberation since it was first proposed in 2003 as a "property tax" (物业税). Key points:

**Legislative requirement**: The property tax cannot be implemented without prior legislation by the National People's Congress. Following the 2013 Third Plenum decision on "tax legality" and the 2015 amendment to the Legislative Law (stipulating that tax types, rates, and collection must be established by law), any future property tax requires full NPC legislative approval.

1. The tax requires a comprehensive redesign of the existing tax and fee system related to real estate and land, which is highly complex.
2. Collection challenges: China's tax collection has almost exclusively targeted legal entities (even personal income tax is withheld by employers), so direct collection from individual residents is unprecedented and costly. In Shanghai and Chongqing's pilot programs (begun 2011), revenue was minimal—Chongqing collected under 400 million yuan over 2011-2013, and Shanghai collected about 600 million yuan over three years—far below collection costs.

**Expert recommendations**: State Council Counselor and Central University of Finance and Economics deputy dean Liu Huan (刘桓) suggests the tax could be delegated to qualified asset appraisal intermediary organizations to save government resources, though he doubts their integrity and capacity are currently sufficient.

Expert Wang Dehua (社科院) notes developed countries typically use assessed value (lower than market price) as the tax base, adjusted every few years. Liu Huan recommends a per-capita exemption of 60 square meters (as in Shanghai's pilot), meaning a family of three could exempt 180 sqm, ensuring first homes are tax-free.

**Relation to land transfer fees**: China's local governments heavily depend on land transfer revenue (2014 national land transfer income exceeded 4 trillion yuan; Shanghai's 2014 land transfer income was ~17.64 billion yuan, about 38.47% of its public fiscal revenue). Shanghai's 2014 residential property tax (~2.76 billion yuan) was only about 1% of its land transfer income. SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article from People's Weekly (人民周刊) discusses China's property tax (房地产税) reform, which has been proposed for 13 years and is now being pushed "without hesitation" (义无反顾) by government officials. Finance Minister Lou Jiwei stated that income tax and property tax reforms have faced obstacles but will be pursued resolutely.

Key points:
- The reform was first proposed in 2003 via the Third Plenary Session of the 16th CPC Central Committee. In 2013, the Third Plenary Session of the 18th Central Committee's "Decision on Major Issues Concerning Comprehensively Deepening Reforms" first called for accelerating property tax legislation.

- Pilot programs began in Shanghai and Chongqing in January 2011.

- Chongqing's pilot: targets luxury homes including villas and high-end homes priced at twice the local average, with rates of 0.5%-1.2%.

Wang Lina (Chinese Academy of Social Sciences economist) said the reform's purpose is to return housing to its residential nature, shifting from transaction-phase taxation to holding-phase taxation to curb speculation and invigorate existing stock.
- Benefits cited: steady revenue for local governments, curbing speculative investment and rapid price increases, and income redistribution amid rising Gini coefficient.

--- SOURCE 4: 特别国债与长期国债的国际比较与经验借鉴 ---
URL: https://fisf.fudan.edu.cn/ffr/content/525

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article, written by 曹萍 (武汉大学访问学者、广东金融学院副教授) and 李湛 (招商基金研究部首席经济学家), examines the international comparison and experience of special long-term government bonds (特别国债与长期国债) to inform China's policy on issuing ultra-long-term special treasury bonds. The article is triggered by China's 2024 Government Work Report, which announced plans to issue ultra-long-term special treasury bonds over several consecutive years (starting with 1 trillion yuan in 2024) to fund major national strategic projects and security capacity building.

**US Treasury Bond Management:**
- At end of 2019, short-term bills comprised 14.5% and medium/long-term bonds 85.5% of US debt. In 2020, COVID relief pushed US fiscal deficit to a record $3.1 trillion, with the Treasury issuing $21 trillion in bonds (of which $17.1 trillion short-term). From 2021, the US resumed increasing medium/long-term issuance to rebalance its maturity structure.
- The US Treasury sells tradable bonds via regularly scheduled public auctions, with participants including the Fed, deposit institutions, individuals, brokers/dealers, pension funds, and foreign investors. The Fed participates via add-on auctions for its SOMA account maturities.
- By 2023, the Fed held ~20% of US Treasuries, the US government ~20% (mostly non-tradable), and international investors' share declined to ~25%.
- Before 2020, US bond management aimed to keep the yield curve non-cyclical to support dollar hegemony. After COVID, the strategy shifted to "long-cycle" management: allowing temporary yield curve distortions in exchange for excess financing, coordinating Fed-Treasury to selectively repair the curve, and gradually restoring the curve long-term.

**Panama Canal Case Study:**
- In 1903, the US signed a treaty with Panama granting exclusive monopoly over the canal (including military, administrative, and judicial rights), paying $10 million upfront plus $250,000 annually after 9 years. In 1911, the US issued 50-year bonds to fund construction, spending $386 million and employing 75,000 workers. The canal opened August 15, 1914, shortening the New York-San Francisco route by 12,600 km.

**Japanese Bond Market:**
- By end-2023, Japan's bond market reached 1,364 trillion yen, with government bonds at 1,136 trillion yen. Since 2013, the Bank of Japan has become the largest holder of Japanese government bonds (over half), but low yields limit foreign investor interest.
- Japanese bond maturities are long, primarily 10- and 20-year; as of end-2022, bonds with 10+ year maturities comprised 75.2% of outstanding, while 1-year-or-less was only 5.8%.

**Japan's 2011 "Reconstruction Special Bonds" Case Study:**
- After the Great East Japan Earthquake, Japan planned 10 trillion yen in reconstruction bonds but only issued ~3 trillion yen (2011-2013) because the Bank of Japan declined to purchase such large volumes. Total reconstruction costs (2011-2022) reached 40.18 trillion yen (~2 trillion RMB), including 13.49 trillion for housing/town rebuilding, 7.86 trillion for Fukushima nuclear disaster recovery, and 6.1 trillion in special delivery taxes to local governments. Japan also imposed a 3-5 year "Reconstruction Tax" raising consumption, income, and corporate taxes.

**China's Long-term Bond Management:**
- Special bonds differ from ordinary bonds in that they serve specific policy purposes, with dedicated budget accounts tracking their use. Whether special bonds count toward fiscal deficit depends on State Council directives — early special bonds and long-term construction bonds counted, while 1998 and 2007 issues were placed in central government funds and did not.
- Since 2001 (first 15- and 20-year ultra-long bonds), China has expanded ultra-long bond issuance. 2009 saw the first 50-year bonds. 2020 issuance of 6,200 billion yuan was a record high. By late January 2024, China's ultra-long bond stock reached 4.96 trillion yuan (17% of total national debt).
- Long-term construction bonds (1998-2007) were directed to agriculture/forestry/water (28%), urban construction (20%), transportation (18%), industrial tech upgrades (10%), rural grid (9%), environmental protection (3%), and education/judicial (3%).

**China's Four Rounds of Special Bonds:**
1. 1989-1991: Special bonds to curb inflation (50/45/20 billion yuan respectively) amid "dual tightening" policy.
2. 1998: Special bonds to recapitalize banks (270 billion yuan subscription) amid Asian Financial Crisis when state banks' NPL ratio exceeded 25% and capital adequacy was ~5%.
3. 2007: Special bonds totaling 1.55 trillion yuan to strengthen foreign exchange reserve management, with 1.35 trillion yuan directed to Agricultural Bank to fund China Investment Corporation (中投公司).
4. 2020: Anti-epidemic special bonds of 1 trillion yuan via market-based issuance, supporting epidemic control, enterprise resumption, infrastructure, and tax/fee reductions.

**Dual Roles of Long-term Bonds:**
- Non-specific purpose bonds: Low global interest rates push governments to issue long bonds for cheaper financing (e.g., Germany's first zero-coupon 30-year bond in 2019; US exploring 50-100 year bonds). Longer bonds enrich instruments for central bank rate intervention, and aging populations/rising life expectancy increase demand for long-duration assets (pension plans, insurers). Per OECD, 14 of 34 member countries have issued sovereign bonds with 40-100 year maturities.
- Specific-purpose bonds serve five functions historically: (1) war bonds (UK 5% WWI bonds, debt reaching £1.285 billion; US WWII bonds of $185.7 billion at 2.9%); (2) crisis support (Japan's special deficit bonds in 1964 post-Olympics and 1975 of ~2 trillion yen); (3) foreign exchange stabilization (South Korea's FXSB of $4.1 billion in 1998, RMB-denominated 3 billion yuan FXSB in 2015); (4) debt restructuring to rebuild sovereign credit (Peru's $2.5 billion in 2010; Argentina's $16.5 billion in 2016); (5) disaster reconstruction (Chile's $1.5 billion after the 2010 8.8-magnitude earthquake).

**Policy Recommendations for China:**
1. Establish clear central-local fiscal relations and increase central government long-term bond issuance to reduce local fiscal pressure.
2. Match bonds with quality projects — invest in technology, frontier infrastructure, and new infrastructure supporting data elements; improve multi-factor project screening.
3. Reasonably control government bond issuance scale to balance with fiscal sustainability, avoiding crowding-out effects.
4. Deepen financial market construction — introduce social security funds, annuities, commercial pension insurance as long-term capital sources; clarify central bank rules for secondary market trading; develop bond futures derivatives.
5. Maintain strict fiscal discipline and hard budget constraints, with accountability to curb blind borrowing and ensure funds are used effectively.
</summary>

<summary>
**中央转移支付 (Central Transfer Payments) - Baidu Baike Encyclopedia Entry**

This webpage is a Baidu Baike encyclopedia entry defining and detailing China's "central transfer payment" (中央转移支付) system — a national fiscal policy implemented to coordinate balanced regional socioeconomic development and ensure equalization of basic public services.

**Definition & Origins:**
- Central transfer payments are China's primary regional compensation policy, used widely worldwide to narrow regional development gaps.
- The system operates by higher-level governments making free (non-repayable) fund allocations to lower-level governments to address regional fiscal imbalances.
- Originated from the 1994 tax-sharing system reform (分税制改革).
- Includes three categories: general transfer payments (均衡财力), special transfer payments (定向支持特定领域), and co-financing transfer payments (共同财政事权, established in 2019).

**Historical Development:**
- 1994: Tax-sharing system reform began; transfer payment system trial implementation to ensure equal access to education, health, and environmental services.
- 2014: State Council pushed reform establishing general transfer payments as the dominant structure.
- 2020: Fiscal fund direct-arrival mechanism created.
- 2023: Central-to-local transfer payments reached 10.06 trillion yuan.

**Key Statistics & Recent Data:**
- 2025: Budget allocated 10.34 trillion yuan (same-caliber growth of 8.4%), focusing on increasing general transfer payments to strengthen local fiscal capacity (announced by Finance Minister Lan Fo'an on March 6, 2025).
- 2025 actual execution: 101,925.14 billion yuan (10.19 trillion), exceeding central-level general public revenue for the first time; third consecutive year above 10 trillion.
- 2026: Budget increased to 10.4 trillion yuan (10.42 trillion), a record high — fourth consecutive year above 10 trillion.
- Six transfer payment methods: tax rebates, original system subsidies, special subsidies, various settlement subsidies, and other subsidies.

**Distribution by Province (2025 execution data):**
- 10 provinces received over 400 billion yuan each, led by: Sichuan (684 billion), Henan (~596.8 billion), Xinjiang (incl. Corps, ~529 billion), Hunan, Hubei, Hebei, Heilongjiang, Yunnan, Anhui, Guangxi.
- Funds primarily flowed to central, western, and northeastern regions; eastern six provinces (Guangdong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Shanghai, Shandong, Beijing) received only ~1.2 trillion total (~12% of total).
- Per-capita transfer payments highest in: Tibet (over 70,000 yuan), Xinjiang, Qinghai, Ningxia, Heilongjiang. Sichuan: 8,200 yuan; Henan: 6,100 yuan; Guangdong (largest economy): only 2,070 yuan — lowest nationally.
- Net contributors: Guangdong, Shanghai, Beijing, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Shandong, Fujian, Tianjin — with Guangdong contributing ~800 billion yuan net in 2025.

**Latest Policy Developments (2025-2026):**
- Since 2024, a "high-quality development incentive fund" of 50 billion yuan annually was added to transfer payments (纳入县级基本财力保障机制奖补资金).

URL: https://economy.caixin.com/2024-07-31/102221775.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a Caixin.com (财新网) news article published on July 31, 2024, reporting on China's Ministry of Finance (MOF) announcement regarding the reform of the consumption tax and local tax system.

**Key Points:**

1. **Main Announcement**: The MOF stated it will consider moving the collection point of the consumption tax (消费税) backward to the retail stage and steadily devolving it to local governments, to be implemented in a staged, item-by-item (分品目、分步骤) manner.

2. **Additional Tax Reforms Announced**:
   - Merging the urban maintenance and construction tax (城市维护建设税), education surcharge (教育费附加), and local education surcharge (地方教育附加) into a single "local surtax" (地方附加税)
   - Adding volatile organic compounds (VOCs/挥发性有机物) to the scope of the environmental protection tax (环保税)

3. **Background Context**: 
   - The announcement follows the Third Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee (二十届三中全会), which outlined reforms to expand local tax sources and increase local fiscal autonomy
   - The plenum's "Decision" document explicitly called for increasing local self-raised fiscal capacity, expanding local tax sources, and appropriately expanding local tax administration authority
   - MOF Vice Minister Wang Dongwei (王东伟) made the remarks at a State Council Information Office press conference on "promoting high-quality development"
   - Wang noted that as China transitions to high-quality development, problems with the current local tax system are becoming increasingly prominent, including an imperfect system, unreasonable structure, and inadequate tax power allocation

4. **Related Issues**: The article also mentions standardizing non-tax revenue management and appropriately delegating some non-tax revenue management authority to localities for differentiated management based on local conditions.

**Author/Publication Details**: Written by Caixin reporter 程思炜 (Cheng Siwei), edited by 于海荣 (Yu Hairong), published on July 31, 2024, under the Economy > News section of Caixin.com.
</summary>

--- SOURCE 2: 田志伟：2025政府工作报告解读——推进消费税征税环节后移 ---
URL: https://cmi.sufe.edu.cn/9c/aa/c12152a236714/page.htm

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a policy analysis article from the Institute for Chinese-style Modernization (中国式现代化研究院) at Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, published on March 6, 2025. The author is Tian Zhiwei (田志伟), a special research fellow at the institute, interpreting two key fiscal reform measures from China's 2025 Government Work Report.

The article analyzes two main topics:

**1. Moving consumption tax collection forward (消费税征收环节后移并下划地方)**

- The 2025 Government Work Report calls for accelerating the shift of consumption tax collection for certain categories from production to wholesale/retail stages, and allocating it to local governments to increase local fiscal autonomy.
- This builds on a 2019 State Council notice and the 2024 Third Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, which both proposed similar reforms.
- The 2019 plan targeted high-end watches, precious jewelry, and jade/gemstones first, but these categories generate limited revenue and cannot solve current local fiscal pressures.
- Consumption tax has 15 categories (烟/含 tobacco, refined oil, automobiles, alcohol), but most revenue comes from four: tobacco, alcohol, refined oil, and automobiles.
- Current collection is at production stage mainly for administrative convenience, but this has caused tax evasion issues (e.g., companies artificially lowering factory prices to related entities).
- From an administrative control perspective, the feasibility ranking for moving collection downstream is: tobacco (best, due to monopoly sales management), automobiles, refined oil, and alcohol (hardest).
- However, since automobiles play a key role in stimulating consumption, moving automobile tax downstream is less likely. The author suggests lowering the threshold for luxury car retail-stage taxation from 1.3 million yuan to 800,000 yuan.

**2. Establishing incentive mechanisms to cultivate local fiscal resources**

- Debates on future local tax systems include property tax, consumption tax, environmental protection tax, and personal income tax as candidates for main local taxes, but none has achieved consensus.
- The author argues that, in the long term, a property tax-based local tax system is most appropriate because it aligns the interests of local governments and residents — governments improve public services to collect more property tax, while residents "vote with their feet" to choose where to live.
- However, this requires institutional support such as lowering transaction costs for residents to move (reducing real estate transaction taxes), to prevent governments from exploiting residents' high relocation costs by lowering public service quality.
- The Government Work Report's call to "actively explore establishing incentive mechanisms" allows local governments to independently explore within limited scope, using decentralization to encourage local governments to actively seek tax sources and relieve fiscal pressure.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
2025年的《政府工作报告》指出要“加快推进部分品目消费税征收环节后移并下划地方，增加地方自主财力”，要“积极探索建立激励机制，促进地方在高质量发展中培育财源”。
</key_excerpts>

URL: https://www.audit.gov.cn/n6/n39/c10784298/content.html

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This webpage is from the official website of the National Audit Office of the People's Republic of China (审计署), specifically from the "Audit Research" (审计科研) section of the "Audit Window" (审计之窗) channel. The page contains a research article titled "消费税征收环节后移并稳步下划地方的推进情况及审计对策建议" (Progress on Shifting the Consumption Tax Collection Stage Backward and Steadily Allocating It to Local Governments, and Audit Countermeasure Suggestions), authored by 戎梅 (Rong Mei) and published on May 9, 2026, by the Audit Research Institute of the National Audit Office.

Key content of the article:
- The consumption tax has been levied since 1994 and has undergone 6 adjustments to its collection stage. Currently, it is primarily collected at the production stage, with all revenue belonging to the central government.
- In 2019, the reform task of shifting the consumption tax collection stage backward and allocating it to local governments was first proposed.
- The 14th Five-Year Plan (2021) and the Third Plenary Session of the 20th CPC Central Committee (2024) made important deployments for this reform.
- The 2025 Government Work Report proposed "accelerating" the consumption tax reform.
- The reform requires completing 4 specific tasks:
  1. Selecting tax items for shifting the collection stage backward based on the principle of controllable collection and management;
  2. Rationally determining the "base year," "base number," and "increment" calculation calibers;
  3. Fully assessing the impact of revenue allocation on local fiscal revenue;
  4. Effectively addressing collection and management challenges related to consumption tax reform.
- Audit recommendations include: tracking reform progress (timeline, roadmap, legislation, and institutional construction); supervising tax collection and management (tax source management and duty performance); and reflecting potential risks during reform (including increased fiscal pressure on some local governments in the early stage and possible unhealthy tax competition among local governments).

The webpage also contains the site's standard navigation menus, including sections for News, Announcements/Reports, Information Disclosure, Audit Window, and Public Interaction, along with the National Audit Office's contact information (address: No. 17 Jinnan Middle Street, Fengtai District, Beijing, 100073).
</summary>

--- SOURCE 5: 岳树民等：消费税制度改革的目标及其实现路径 - 财税研究所 ---
URL: http://ipft.ruc.edu.cn/yjcg/sdpl/5c30ea5c2e4d43e8bf0673853fa7b34a.htm

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This article, published in the "International Taxation" (《国际税收》) journal's 2025 issue No. 8, is authored by Yue Shumin (岳树民), a professor at Renmin University of China's School of Finance and a senior researcher at the Finance and Taxation Research Institute, and Wang Li (王荔), a doctoral student at Renmin University of China. The article examines the goals, implementation paths, challenges, and countermeasures for China's consumption tax (excise duty) system reform.

KEY CONTENT:

**Historical Background:** China's consumption tax (特别消费税/Excise Duty) was established in 1994 as a special consumption tax levied on selected consumer goods on top of VAT, primarily to regulate consumption structure, control pollution, protect the environment, and secure fiscal revenue. Major reforms occurred in 2003 (expanding the tax base), 2013 (adjusting tax scope, categories, and rates, including high energy-consuming and high-pollution products), 2016 (imposing consumption tax on ultra-luxury cars at retail stage), 2019 (State Council plan to move consumption tax collection to later stages and devolve it to local governments), and 2024 (the 20th CPC Central Committee's Third Plenary Session explicitly proposed "advancing the backward movement of consumption tax collection stages and steadily devolving it to local governments").

**Key Statistics:** In 2023, domestic consumption tax revenue was approximately 1.6 trillion yuan (8.9% of total tax revenue), while domestic VAT was about 6.9 trillion yuan (38% of total tax revenue), a ratio of roughly 1:4 (compared to OECD's ~1:3 ratio). In 2023, central government fiscal expenditure accounted for 13.9% and local government 86.1%, while central revenue was 45.9% and local 54.1%. Local fiscal revenue was about 11.7 trillion yuan, with local autonomous revenue of about 5.06 trillion yuan (43.2%).

**Reform Goals:** (1) Enhance regulatory functions; (2) Enhance revenue functions; (3) Establish a foundation for improving central-local fiscal relations by increasing local autonomous fiscal capacity.

**Implementation Paths:** (1) Appropriately expand the tax base (including high-sugar/high-fat/high-salt foods, high energy-consuming/polluting goods, high-substitution resource-energy goods, and some luxury goods); (2) Optimize tax rate structure (higher rates for non-green goods with substitutes and suppressed goods; moderate rates for luxury goods; lower rates for widely consumed goods; minimize rate tiers for administrability); (3) Move collection from production/import stage to wholesale/retail stage, advancing step-by-step ("条件合适" for collection stage movement, "过程稳妥" for revenue devolution).

**Challenges:** (1) Tax compliance issues from moving collection to wholesale/retail (especially for small businesses and individual proprietors); (2) Tax administration difficulties (more dispersed taxpayers, higher management costs); (3) Multi-sales-model and multi-business-format management issues (e.g., online direct sales, platform sales, distinguishing wholesale from retail, consumption location determination); (4) New interest incentive mechanisms from revenue devolution (potential regional fiscal imbalances, risk of local governments encouraging consumption of restricted goods).

**Proposed Countermeasures:** (1) Adopt a "small steps" approach—advance reforms selectively for goods with clear identification and controllability (e.g., tobacco, alcohol, gold/silver jewelry, high-end cosmetics, high-end watches); (2) Use a systematic perspective to coordinate VAT and consumption tax reforms, establish transitional transfer payment mechanisms, and carefully time the devolution of revenues from strongly-suppressed goods like cigarettes (which already have established social constraints against consumption); (3) Improve compliance and administration through digital tax management systems (including government-provided digital systems for small businesses and smart tax systems using product identity codes and information-sharing platforms, drawing on the refined oil industry's management model); (4) Give appropriate consideration to small businesses and individual proprietors—recommending consumption tax exemption aligned with VAT threshold policies for ordinary daily-goods shops, but not for specialized sellers of tobacco, alcohol, luxury watches, gold/jewelry, etc.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"推进消费税征收环节后移并稳步下划地方"是我国新一轮财税体制改革的重要任务，兼具健全现代税收制度、增强地方自主财力、完善中央地方财政关系等多重目的。—党的二十届三中全会改革要求
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 6: 赵波：如何理解财政部“年内不具备扩大房地产税改革试点城市的条件”？ ---
URL: https://www.bimba.pku.edu.cn/wm/xwzx/xwlx/jsgd/522194.htm

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is an opinion/analysis article by Zhao Bo (赵波), Associate Professor of Economics (tenured) at Peking University National School of Development (BiMBA), published April 6, 2022, explaining why China's Ministry of Finance announced that it would not expand property tax reform pilot cities in 2022, despite the National People's Congress having authorized such pilots in October 2021.

Key arguments for delaying the expansion:
1. Property tax revenue is enormous with strong contractionary and multiplier effects. Housing assets account for 2.3 times China's GDP (Li Yang & Zhang Xiaojing, 2020). A uniform 0.6% tax rate would yield tax revenue equal to 1.4% of GDP (~1.6 trillion yuan based on 2021 GDP), exceeding individual income tax or consumption tax shares of GDP. Alternative scenarios (taxing homes over 3 million yuan, homes over 60 sqm per capita, or third+ homes) would yield 0.44%, 0.2%, and 0.2% of GDP respectively.

2. Delaying helps stabilize consumption—China faces "demand contraction, supply shocks, and weakening expectations" (2021 Central Economic Work Conference), and consumption has contributed over 50% of GDP growth for 11 consecutive years. Omicron outbreaks and lockdowns further pressure consumption.

3. Delaying reduces short-term real estate market instability. Shanghai's pilot reduced property investment but not prices; Chongqing's pilot reduced prices but not investment. The real estate sector is in a "severe winter" with sluggish investment and sales, tight developer cash flows. The March 16, 2022 State Council Financial Stability and Development Committee meeting called for risk resolution measures.

4. Delaying supports the 2022 tax-and-fee reduction targets (~2.5 trillion yuan), as property tax collection would offset these efforts.

Problems with rolling out property tax nationally:
- Large regional heterogeneity requiring city-specific policies (high housing price-to-income ratios in developed cities face heavier burdens)
- Unresolved question of whether revenue stays local (which would worsen regional inequality) or is centrally coordinated with transfer payments
- Significant social wealth redistribution effects differing for owner-occupiers, investors (helps achieve "housing without speculation"), and renters (via spillover effects), plus disproportionate impact on elderly populations with higher housing price-to-income ratios

Conclusion: The delay reflects a tradeoff between counter-cyclical (short-term) and cross-cyclical (structural) policy adjustments. Since expectations of future property tax already shape behavior, delaying implementation is equivalent to "implementing the tax but deferring collection"—structural adjustment may still occur through expectations. The author cites evidence (Du & Zhang, 2015) that Chongqing's pilot reduced housing price growth by 2.52%, while Shanghai's pilot had no significant effect on prices.
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"房地产税税收巨大，对于经济有着巨大的紧缩效果和乘数效应。房屋资产为占我国居民财富比重最大的资产，总计GDP的2.3倍（李扬、张晓晶，2020）。"
</key_excerpts>

2. **Local government authority**: The reform would conditionally grant local governments the power to set real estate tax rates within a certain range, increasing local fiscal flexibility and autonomy.

3. **Expected benefits**: The tax is expected to help establish new home-buying concepts, promote the rental housing market, reduce tax burdens for most ordinary citizens, help local governments achieve fiscal balance (reducing reliance on unsustainable "land finance" or land sale revenue), and support self-occupancy housing demand while curbing speculative investment.

--- SOURCE 8: 中国经济：地方政府财政危机下仍未推房地产税背后有何争议？ - BBC ---
URL: https://www.bbc.com/zhongwen/simp/chinese-news-66797074

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This BBC Chinese article (published September 15, 2023) examines why China's property tax (房地产税) has been shelved despite local government fiscal crises stemming from declining land-sale revenues. Key points:

**Context:** China's economic recovery after pandemic restrictions was weak, especially in real estate. On September 6, 2023, the 14th National People's Congress Standing Committee released its five-year legislative plan, which did NOT include the property tax law in any of its three categories (79 draft laws ready for review, 51 needing further work, and items requiring continued research). This surprised observers because a draft had already circulated for comments in 2021, and in October 2021 the NPC authorized the State Council to pilot property tax reforms in selected regions.

**Why the property tax was proposed:** China's 20-year real estate boom saw both developers over-borrowing and local governments earning huge revenues from land sales. When asset returns couldn't cover interest, Ponzi-style "borrowing new to repay old" financing emerged. In 2020, policies cooling the property market led to crises at Evergrande, Country Garden, and others, with local government land-transfer revenues sharply declining. The property tax was seen as an ideal replacement revenue source for land-dependent local finances. Additionally, after the business tax-to-VAT reform under Xi Jinping, local governments had fewer tax sources and needed a self-controlled tax. Xi also framed the property tax as serving "common prosperity" (共同富裕) to prevent polarization, writing about this in the party journal Qiushi.

**Timeline of attempts:**
- 2011: First pilot property taxes launched in Shanghai (targeting multi-home residents) and Chongqing (targeting high-end luxury homes)
- 2017: Then-Finance Minister Xiao Jie set a timeline for completing legislative procedures by 2019 and implementation by 2020 — this failed
- October 23, 2021: NPC Standing Committee authorized the State Council to conduct property tax reform pilots in certain regions, covering residential and non-residential properties, with a five-year pilot period — but no further action followed
- 2023: Latest legislative plan omits the property tax entirely, suggesting no implementation for at least five more years

**Current context:** In June-July 2023, sales by China's 100 largest developers fell about 30% year-on-year. In late July, the Politburo meeting unusually omitted the "housing is for living, not speculation" (房住不炒) phrase, signaling easing. On August 25, 2023, regulators issued the "recognition of housing not loans" (认房不认贷) policy easing first-home mortgage rules. Launching a property tax now could disrupt this fragile recovery.

**Controversies and expert views:**
- Double taxation: Residents already pay for 70-year land use rights; taxing them again constitutes double taxation since transaction-phase taxes (land value-added tax, urban construction tax, farmland occupation tax) are already passed on to buyers
- Legal issue: China's land is state-owned, not private, unlike Western property tax systems where property is privately owned — so taxing land arguably should be paid by the state (landowner), not residents
- Former State Taxation Administration deputy director Xu Shanda noted two difficulties: (1) land values appreciate while buildings depreciate, making a unified tax base hard; (2) land is state-owned while buildings are privately owned, making a unified tax on two different subjects challenging
- CUHK Associate Professor Yang Yang said in oversupplied cities property prices could fall, but in first-tier cities where demand exceeds supply, prices unlikely to drop — the tax would just be passed on to buyers or rents
</summary>

<key_excerpts>
"在制定房地产税的时候，因为必然要包括地税，怎么样整合或降低前期建设和交易环节的税收来避免重复征税，其实也是政府在制定新政策时面临的一个问题" - 杨扬（香港中文大学副教授）; "推进房地产税的立法有两个难点：一方面，随着时间的推移，土地价值在升值，而房屋在贬值，税基难以统一；另一方面，土地属于国有，而房屋属于私有，一个统一的税如何对两个不同的纳税主体征收，也是重大的挑战" - 许善达（原国家税务总局副局长）; 杨扬：如果征收房产税，在房产供过于求的城市，房价可能出现下降的情况；但在一线城市，住房需求远远大于供给，房价不太可能下降; "不会因为骂声而改变" - 时任财政部长肖捷（2017年）关于推进房产税的表态
</key_excerpts>

--- SOURCE 1: 地方化债“成绩单”揭晓，“下降”成关键词，凸显在五大方面 ---
URL: https://m.cls.cn/detail/1601159

SUMMARY:
<summary>
This is a news article from 财联社 (Cailian Press) dated February 23, 2024, reporting on the 2023 local government debt resolution ("化债") achievements across China, based on a review of 2024 government work reports from 31 provinces and 86 cities/counties, combined with 2023 budget execution drafts and 2024 budget drafts.

**2023 Key Achievements (Five Main Trends):**
1. **Debt risk level downgrades**: The Ministry of Finance classifies local debt risk into four tiers (Red ≥300% debt ratio, Orange 200-300%, Yellow 120-200%, Green <120%). Examples: Inner Mongolia's Alxa and Wuhai cities and 8 banner/county governments exited Orange; Baotou exited Red; Hubei Huanggang and Inner Mongolia's Zhuozi County exited Orange; Jiangsu province maintained Green; Yancheng turned Green; Liaoning's Nanfen District moved from Yellow to Green for the first time.

2. **Debt scale and debt ratio declines**: Ningxia achieved "three declines" (debt scale, debt ratio, risk level) with record resolution efforts; Guangxi saw significant reduction in implicit debt; Gansu resolved 104.84 billion yuan of financing platform debt. According to Guangfa Fixed Income chief Liu Yu, 23 provinces saw slower growth in interest-bearing debt of bond-issuing city investment companies by Q3 2023. Jilin, Tibet and Guizhou saw declines exceeding 50 percentage points; Yunnan, Chongqing and Gansu saw declines of 40-50 percentage points. Financing costs also fell—Changde, Hunan lowered average annual interest rates on existing debt to ~5%, Xiangtan to below 4%.

3. **Special refinancing bonds**: From September 2023, a new round of special refinancing bonds was issued, totaling nearly 1.4 trillion yuan. In Q4, the National People's Congress Standing Committee approved 1 trillion yuan in additional national bonds managed as special bonds. Xiangtan, Hunan secured 65.09 billion yuan—the largest amount among prefecture-level cities disclosed. Other recipients included Zhuzhou's Lukou District (3.194 billion yuan total across multiple bond types), Bazhong, Sichuan (1.8 billion yuan), Jiang'an County, Yibin (2.4 billion yuan, top in the province among counties), and Tonghai County, Yunnan (432 million yuan).

4. **Implicit debt resolution pilots**: Multiple cities/counties obtained implicit debt resolution pilot status, including Loudi, Hunan (city level and Lengshuijiang City approved as national pilots), Gaogang District in Taizhou, Jiangsu, and Anyue County in Ziyang, Sichuan.

5. **Reduction in financing platform numbers**: Henan pushed to strip government financing functions from platforms with orderly reductions; Chongqing's Fuling District reduced 19 state-owned enterprises with 7 platform SOEs clearing implicit debt; Nanjing's Qinhuai District reduced platform numbers by 15.

**2024 Plans:**
- Focus on "implementing" debt resolution measures: strengthening risk monitoring, implementing financial support for debt resolution, and promoting platform transformation.
- Jiangxi and Yunnan will use "one debt, one strategy" approaches; Fujian, Shaanxi and Henan will target high-risk regions; Jilin will optimize debt structure and reduce costs.
